**Eutychianus**, bishop of Basti, took part in the Council of Illiberis. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 5.

[Col. 1247] **Eutychius**, martyr of Asta in Spain. Dexter, A.C. 112. Eutychius was raised from the dead by the Apostle Paul. Ibid. He suffers martyrdom at Telae. Ibid., and Dexter, A.C. 299.

**Eutychius**, martyr of Salamanca, with his companions. Dexter, A.C. 430.

**Many martyrs named Eutychius in Spain:** how many? Commentary, A.C. 112, no. 3.

**When was the door of the Gospel opened to the Gentiles, and what does this mean?** Commentary, A.C. 36, at length.

**In what year did Matthew write the Gospel?** Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 37, no. 7.

**From whom was the Gospel dictated by John taken down?** Commentary, A.C. 94, no. 3.

**Eventius**, a martyr of Caesaraugusta, one of the eighteen companions. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 50.

**Evexes**, a Carthaginian presbyter, took part in the Council of Illiberis in place of his bishop. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 5.

**Exuperantius of Uxama** was transferred to Ravenna. Dexter, A.C. 385; A.C. 388; and A.C. 407.

## F

**Fabian**, pope. Dexter, A.C. 255.

**Fabricianus**, abbot and martyr, with a companion, at Titulcia. Dexter, A.C. 308; Commentary, no. 6.

**Facundus**, martyr with his brother Primitivus. Dexter, A.C. 139.

**Faetadius**, bishop of Toledo. Dexter, A.C. 424 and 428.

**Favorinus**, rhetorician. Dexter, A.C. 135.

**Faustina Augusta**, disciple of Saint Catherine, suffers martyrdom. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 60.

**Faustinus**, a noble citizen of Pamplona, converted to the faith. Commentary, A.C. 110, no. 3.

**Faustus**, martyr with Januarius and Martialis. Commentary, A.C. 299, at the end.

**Faustus**, martyr of Caesaraugusta, one of the eighteen companions. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 50.

**Faustus**, martyr of Clunia, with his companions. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 63.

**Febronia**, virgin and martyr in Syria. Dexter, A.C. 308; Commentary, no. 1.

**Felicianus**, bishop of Málaga and martyr. Dexter, A.C. 308; Commentary, no. 14.

**Felicissima**, martyr and companion of Gracilianus: where was she killed? Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 230, no. 2.

**Felicissimus**, presbyter of Atubi, took part in the Council of Illiberis. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 5.

**Felicula**, martyr and companion of Saints Vitalis and Zeno. Dexter, A.C. 110.

**Felix**, presbyter of Vallata-Urbicua, writes to Saint Cyprian. Dexter, A.C. 255. He was not bishop of Caesaraugusta, indeed not a bishop at all. Commentary, ibid.

**Felix**, martyr and disciple of Saint Irenaeus, with his companions. Dexter, A.C. 255.

**Felix**, bishop, sent with Sabinus to Saint Cyprian. Commentary, A.C. 255, no. 2.

**Felix**, martyr and companion of Saint Regula, killed at Turigium. Dexter, A.C. 285.

**Felix**, martyr and companion of Januarius, killed at Heraclea. Dexter, A.C. 296.

**Felix**, bishop of Acci, presides over the Council of Illiberis. Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 5.

**Felix**, archdeacon of Toledo, compiled the canons of the Council of Illiberis. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 12. Finally he is crowned with martyrdom at Seville. Ibid., in the Commentary, and Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 48.

**Felix**, martyr of Carthage, with his companions. Commentary, A.C. 270, no. 2.

**Felix**, martyr of Ebura in Carpetania, [Col. 1248] with his companions. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 20. Another Felix of Ebura. Ibid.

**Felix**, martyr of Patavonium, with his companions. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 34.

**Felix**, martyr of Gerunda. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 21, and especially Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 43.

**Two Felix martyrs of Gerunda.** Commentary, A.C. 277, no. 2.

**Felix**, bishop and martyr of Carthage, with his companions. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 47.

**Felix**, martyr of Caesaraugusta, one of the eighteen companions. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 50.

**Felix**, martyr of Clunia, with his companions. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 47.

**Felix**, martyr of Tarragona, with his companions. Commentary, A.C. 360, no. 4.

**Felix the Confessor**, companion of Saint Eulalia of Emerita. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 52, in her life.

**Felix**, martyr of Caparra, with a companion. Dexter, A.C. 360.

**The Fenarium River.** Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 308, no. 6.

**The feast of Saint James**, celebrated in Spain: from what time? Commentary, A.C. 42, no. 4.

**Festus**, martyr of Clunia, with his companions. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 63.

**The faith is vigorously spread throughout Spain.** Dexter, A.C. 100; Commentary, no. 13.

**Profession of faith made by the Fathers of the Council of Braga.** Commentary, A.C. 423, no. 6, in chapter 2 of its Acts.

**Fides**, virgin and martyr of Civitas, or Emerita, suffered at Agaunum. Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 1.

**Firminus**, bishop of Pamplona and of Toulouse. Commentary, A.C. 76, no. 2. He preaches throughout Spain and suffers martyrdom. Dexter, A.C. 110. His deeds are in the Commentary.

**Firmus**, martyr killed at Mellaria. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 14.

**Firmus**, senator of Pamplona, converted to the faith. Commentary, A.C. 110, no. 3. He was the father of Saint Firminus.

**Flacilla**, a most noble Spanish woman. Commentary, A.C. 388, no. 9.

**Flavia Domitilla**, most noble and a martyr. Dexter, A.C. 91. There were two of this name. Commentary, ibid. One suffers martyrdom with her companions. Ibid. The other, however—Dexter, A.C. 100; Commentary, no. 12.

**Flaviobriga**, which city was it? Commentary, A.C. 185, no. 3, and Commentary, A.C. 270, no. 1. Its martyrs. Ibid., and in Dexter.

**Many cities were once distinguished by the name Flavia.** Commentary, A.C. 185, no. 3.

**Flavium Brigantium**, which city was it? Ibid.

**Flavius Lucius Dexter.** See Dexter.

**Flavius**, bishop of Illiberis, took part in the Council of Illiberis. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 5.

**Florentius of Seville**, called M. Bolanus Florentius. Dexter, A.C. 110. Another. Commentary, ibid. He suffers martyrdom. Dexter, A.C. 116.

**Florentius**, bishop of Emerita, takes part in the Council of Córdoba. Dexter, A.C. 356.

**Florian**, emperor. Dexter, A.C. 277.

**Florianus**, martyr of Ebura, with his companions. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 20.

**Forcatus**, bishop of Lugo, renowned for holiness. Dexter, A.C. 385.

**Fortunatus**, martyr and disciple of Saint Irenaeus, with his companions. Dexter, A.C. 255.

**Fortunatus**, martyr at Uxama Barca, with his companions. Dexter, A.C. 268; Commentary, no. 6.

[Col. 1249] **Fortunatus**, citizen of Pamplona, converted to the faith. Commentary, A.C. 110, no. 3.

**Fortunatus**, martyr of Ebura in Carpetania, with his companions. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 20.

**Fortunatus**, martyr of Patavonium, with his companions. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 34.

**Fortunatus**, martyr of Caparra, with a companion. Dexter, A.C. 360.

**Fotinus**, martyr of Clunia, with his companions. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 63.

**Fronto of Périgueux**, bishop. Dexter, A.C. 66; Commentary, no. 13.

**Fronto**, martyr of Caesaraugusta, one of the eighteen companions. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 50.

**Fructuosus**, bishop and martyr of Tarragona, with his companions. Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 268, no. 4.

**The soldiers of the Thunderbolt Legion** included many Spaniards. Commentary, A.C. 175, no. 3.

**Fulta**, bishop of Barcelona. Dexter, A.C. 212.

**Fuscus**, a Spanish charioteer of the Blue faction. Commentary, A.C. 120.

## G

**Gabinus**, emperor. Dexter, A.C. 241.

**Gabrum**, a city. See Egabrum.

**The temple and tomb of Hercules at Cádiz.** Commentary, A.C. 66, no. 22.

**Galba** becomes emperor in Spain. Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 70.

**Galen the Physician.** Dexter, A.C. 141.

**Galerius Maximianus.** See Maximianus.

**Gallienus**, emperor. Dexter, A.C. 268 and Commentary, no. 5, and Dexter, A.C. 270.

**Galla Placidia Augusta**, the same as Placidia, daughter of Theodosius. See Placidia, and Commentary, A.C. 423, no. 1.

**From where are the Gallaeci so called, and from whom did they originate?** Commentary, A.C. 138, no. 5. They were possessed by the Suebi. Dexter, A.C. 423.

**Saint James the Apostle evangelizes Gaul.** Dexter, A.C. 41.

**Gallus**, emperor. Dexter, A.C. 256.

**Gavianus**, martyr of Ebura, with his companions. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 20.

**Gelduba**, a city not in Thrace but in Turdetania. Commentary, A.C. 94, no. 1. Its martyr. Ibid.

**Gemella**, a city. See Augusta-Gemella.

**Gemianus**, a distinguished writer. Dexter, A.C. 230.

**Gemma-Marina.** See Marina the virgin.

**Genesius**, a Mantuan martyr, flourishes at Lisbon with his companions. Dexter, A.C. 308; Commentary, no. 12. He suffers martyrdom. Dexter, A.C. 353.

**Genivera**, virgin and martyr of Tui, with her sisters. Commentary, A.C. 138, no. 5.

**How many geographers, and which ones, did the Elucidator examine?** Part I of the Apology, § 3.

**Georgius**, presbyter and companion of Saint Fronto. Commentary, A.C. 66, no. 13.

**Germana**, a Spanish virgin and martyr, with her sisters. Commentary, A.C. 138, no. 5.

**The Germans ravage Gaul and Italy.** Dexter, A.C. 268.

**Germanus**, martyr of Emerita, with his brother Servandus. Commentary, A.C. 298.

**Geronius**, martyr of Caracena, with a companion. Dexter, A.C. 86.

**Gerontius**, bishop and martyr of Italica. Commentary, A.C. 86, at the end, where there is a hymn in his praise.

**Who buried the bodies of Gervasius and Protasius?** Dexter, A.C. 91.

**Who was the Gervasius who preached in Spain?** Ibid., in the Commentary. [Col. 1249]

**Martyrs of Gerunda.** Commentary, A.C. 277, no. 2.

Cucuphas. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 21.

Felix. Ibid.

Felix and Maximus. Ibid.; Commentary, no. 22.

**Getulius**, father of the seven martyred brothers and a disciple of the Apostle Saint John. Dexter, A.C. 100; Commentary, no. 24.

**Glabrio**, Roman consul, suffers for Christ. Dexter, A.C. 91.

**Origin of the Gnostics.** Dexter, A.C. 136. They multiply in Spain. Dexter, A.C. 380.

**Gonciolum**, a city, the same as Berella. See Berella.

**Gordian**, emperor. Dexter, A.C. 241 and 243. He is killed in A.C. 244.

**The Goths rampage throughout the empire.** Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 38. When did they come to Spain? Dexter, A.C. 424. See the Commentary. They ravage Carpetania. Dexter, A.C. 429, and Complutum, ibid., no. 7, and Mecon, ibid., no. 10. They are the fourth beast of Daniel. See the Appendix to A.C. 430.

**How many Gothic kings were in Spain before Leovigild?** Ibid.

**Gracilianus**, martyr and companion of Felicissima: where was he killed? Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 230, no. 2.

**The Greek Menologion.** See Menologion.

**The Greeks founded many cities in Spain, and which ones?** Commentary, A.C. 138, no. 5.

**The heavenly treasure of Mount Granada** corresponds to Dexter’s Chronicle. Part I of the Apology, § 1, and Commentary, A.C. 57. Concerning the books found there, ibid. What do they say about the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin? Commentary, A.C. 308, no. 9. What judgment should be formed concerning the book in the Spanish language? Commentary, A.C. 54, no. 9.

**Granada**, the city: from where did its name come, and by whom was it founded? Ibid., no. 6.

**Gratian**, bishop of Carthage. Dexter, A.C. 353.

**Gratian**, emperor. Dexter, A.C. 375 and 382. He strongly favors the faith. Ibid. He is killed in A.C. 384.

**Gratus**, martyr of Tarragona, with his companions. Commentary, A.C. 360, no. 4.

**Gregory of Nazianzus** writes to Olympius, bishop of Toledo. Dexter, A.C. 352. And against the heretics. Dexter, A.C. 370.

**Gregory**, bishop of Toledo and successor of Olympius. Dexter, A.C. 356. His distinguished deeds. Ibid. He was a companion of Saint Lucifer of Cagliari, not Gregory the Baetican, or Illiberitanian. Ibid., in the Commentary. He shares exile with Hilary of Poitiers. Dexter, A.C. 360. He dies. Dexter, A.C. 366. He is numbered among the saints. Ibid. He was from Complutum. Commentary, A.C. 94, no. 1.

**Gregory**, bishop of Córdoba, took part in the Council of Milan. Dexter, A.C. 384. He read the names of the martyrs daily at Mass; from this the Martyrologies were composed. Ibid., in the Commentary. See also Dexter, A.C. 424 and A.C. 430.

**Gregory of Illiberis**, formerly prefect of the praetorium of Gaul. Dexter, A.C. 388 and 407. He dies. Dexter, A.C. 423. He wrote a book on the faith. Ibid.

**Gregory**, junior bishop of Córdoba. Dexter, A.C. 388.

**Ulfilas**, bishop of the Goths and inventor of Gothic letters. Dexter, A.C. 380.

**Gudennes**, a Carthaginian virgin and martyr. Dexter, A.C. 208.

## H

**Heresy.** See the Manichaeans, Gnostics, Priscillianists, and Vigilantius.

**Hadria**, martyr of Castulo, with a companion. Dexter, A.C. 66; Commentary, no. 7.

**Hadrian**, emperor. Dexter, A.C. 121, [Col. 1250] and 125, 128, 134, 135, and 139. He was a Spaniard. Commentary, A.C. 188, no. 9.

**Halotus**, Nero’s judge. See Alotus.

**The Jerusalem Hebrews send envoys throughout the whole world** to precede and oppose the apostles. Commentary, A.C. 35, no. 7. They called Christians atheists. Ibid. They shared Christ’s punishment with the Spanish Hebrews, but the latter dissented from them. Ibid.; and A.C. 37, Commentary, no. 9. It is proved at length that they were first brought into Spain by Nabuzardan, minister of Nebuchadnezzar, at the time of the first destruction of Jerusalem. Commentary, A.C. 37, no. 5. Which cities did they establish there? Ibid.

**Helena**, queen of the Adiabenians, becomes a Christian. Dexter, A.C. 66; Commentary, no. 12.

**Helena**, a Spanish martyr. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 29.

**Helena**, mother of the Emperor Constantine. Dexter, A.C. 311. At her urging, churches are erected to Christ throughout the world. Dexter, A.C. 312. She arranges for the feast of the Cross to be instituted. Commentary, A.C. 424, no. 12.

**Heliopolis**, a city in Spain, the same as Solia. Commentary, A.C. 308, no. 7.

**Heliades.** See below.

**Helpidius**, son of Helpidius, flourishes. Dexter, A.C. 385. See Commentary.

**Hemeterius**, martyr of Calagurris. See Emeterius.

**How many cities named Heraclea were there, and which ones?** Commentary, A.C. 70, no. 2.

**Martyrs of Heraclea in Spain.** Dexter, A.C. 296; and A.C. 300, Commentary, no. 35.

**Heraclius**, martyr of Carthage, with Zosimus. Dexter, A.C. 268; Commentary, no. 10.

**Heraclius**, martyr of Augustodunum, with his companions. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 29.

**The temple and tomb of the Egyptian Hercules in Spain.** Commentary, A.C. 66, no. 22.

**Hermenegild**, king of Spain and martyr. Appendix to A.C. 430.

**Hermogenes**, a disciple of Saint James. Commentary, A.C. 42, no. 2. He went to Spain. Ibid. He suffered at Syracuse. Ibid.

**Hermolaus**, prelate and martyr of Toledo, companion and teacher of Saint Acacius and the ten thousand martyrs crucified on Mount Ararat in Armenia. Dexter, A.C. 134. His relics were brought to Toledo. Commentary, ibid.

**The bitter death of Herod**, the king who killed the infants. Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 6. In what year did he order them killed? Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 3.

**The exile and unhappy death of Herod Antipas and Herodias**, his adulterous wife. Both died at Lérida in Catalonia. Dexter, A.C. 34.

**Herod**, martyr of Ebura, with his companions. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 20.

**Herotes, or Herodes**, bishop of Tortosa, sends Orosius to Augustine. Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 400, no. 2.

**Heliades**, companion of Saint Acacius and the ten thousand martyrs. Commentary, A.C. 134, no. 3.

**Hesychius**, martyr of Dorostorum. Commentary, A.C. 168.

**This Chronicle is attributed to Jerome.** See Dexter’s letter to Orosius. In what year did he write the book On Illustrious Men? Part I of the Apology, § 2. His letter to Chromatius and Heliodorus, and their letter to him concerning the publication of the Martyrology, are defended. Commentary, A.C. 384, no. 3. He was a cardinal presbyter. Ibid. See A.C. 385, no. 2. He writes against Vigilantius. Dexter, A.C. [Col. 1251] 388. In what year did he die? Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 426.

**Jerome de la Higuera**, promulgator of this codex: how great a man was he? Part I of the Apology, § 1.

**Hierotheus**, a disciple of Paul, born in Spain, flourished at Athens as a judge of the Areopagus; afterward he was the first bishop of Athens and finally bishop of Segovia. Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 71, no. 3. His writings and spirit. Ibid., in the Commentary. Was he present at the Virgin’s funeral? Commentary, A.C. 48. The recent discovery of his head. Commentary, A.C. 71.

**The Jewish war.** Dexter, A.C. 66. Its destruction. Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 71.

**Higuera.** See Jerome de la Higuera.

**Higinius**, bishop of Córdoba, unruly. Commentary, A.C. 360, no. 9. He is punished by exile. Dexter, A.C. 384. He had previously persecuted Priscillianus fiercely. Commentary, ibid., no. 5. He had Gregory as his successor in the episcopate. Dexter, A.C. 388.

**Hilarion**, martyr of Serpa, with a companion. Dexter, A.C. 308; Commentary, no. 2.

**Hilary of Poitiers.** Dexter, A.C. 353 and 360.

**Himerius**, bishop of Tarragona, convenes a council at Tarragona. Commentary, A.C. 388, no. 10.

**Hippolytus**, an illustrious writer. Dexter, A.C. 230.

**Hippolytus**, martyr of Carthage, with his companions. Dexter, A.C. 270. Another of the same name and city, with his companions. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 47.

**Hippo**, a city of Carpetania: which city was it? Commentary, A.C. 222, no. 2. Its martyrs. Dexter, ibid., and A.C. 285.

**Hiscius.** See Iscius, or Isicius, a disciple of Saint James.

**The Church of Seville**, erected by Saint James, who appointed Saint Pius as its first bishop. Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 37, no. 8. Its prelate consecrates a shrine to the Mother of God. Dexter, A.C. 38, no. 3. Its martyrs. Dexter, A.C. 60, 110, and 115; and Commentary, A.C. 300, nos. 4, 28, and 48. Its bishop took part in the First Council of Nicaea. Dexter, A.C. 324.

**Spanish soldiers** were always exceptionally brave. Commentary, A.C. 34, no. 3. Many were selected as praetorians of the emperors. Ibid.

**From whom did Spain first receive news of Christ’s affairs?** Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 35.

**Spanish Gentiles addressed Christ through Philip’s intervention.** Dexter, ibid.; Commentary, no. 9. The Jews did not consent to Christ’s death. Ibid., no. 7; and Dexter, A.C. 37, Commentary, no. 9. They sent envoys to the Apostle Peter, and for what reason? Dexter, A.C. 35; Commentary, no. 7.

**Spain**, the first of the world’s provinces to be converted to Christ. Dexter, A.C. 36. It was called Sepharad by the Hebrews. Commentary, A.C. 37, no. 5.

**Some Spaniards were present in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.** Commentary, A.C. 35, no. 3.

**Saint Caecilius**, divinely and prophetically instructed in the Spanish language. Commentary, A.C. 54.

**Spanish and Gallic bishops** at the Council of Suessa. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 18.

**Spanish martyrs under Diocletian**, whose names do not survive. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 40.

**Spanish bishops who took part with Hosius in the Council of Nicaea.** Dexter, A.C. 324.

**Praises of Spain**, from the Latin Pacatus and others. Commentary, A.C. 382, no. 10, and Commentary, A.C. 388, no. 9.

**The dispute among Spanish bishops concerning the penance to be granted to the Priscillianists.** Dexter, A.C. 323.

**Their steadfastness during the Gothic invasion**, praised by Augustine. Commentary, A.C. 423, no. 6, at the end. [Col. 1251]

**The Catholic monarchy of the Spanish kings:** when was it founded? Appendix to A.C. 430.

**Honestus**, a presbyter, preaches at Pompeiopolis. Commentary, A.C. 76, no. 2, and Commentary, A.C. 110, no. 3.

**Honoratus**, bishop of Toledo and successor of Saint Eugenius the martyr. Dexter, A.C. 132. He dies. Commentary, A.C. 140.

**Honorius**, martyr of Asta. Dexter, A.C. 112.

**Honorius**, emperor and son of Theodosius. Commentary, A.C. 388, no. 9.

**Honorius**, father of monks. Dexter, A.C. 424.

**What does Hormestra signify?** It is the genuine title of Orosius’s book. Commentary, A.C. 417, no. 1.

**Hosius of Córdoba**, compiler of the canons of the Council of Illiberis. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 12. Much is said about him. Ibid., no. 5. He arranges for churches to be built throughout the world. Dexter, A.C. 312. He was especially dear to Constantine and Helena. Ibid., and in the Commentary. He presides over the Council of Nicaea and composes the Creed of the Mass. Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 324, no. 1. He is acquitted by the Council of Arles. Commentary, A.C. 311, no. 1. His most holy letters to Constantius. Commentary, A.C. 356, no. 1. Concerning him. Commentary, A.C. 356, no. 3. He dies a holy death. Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 360, no. 2. His feast day, celebrated by the Syrian Church as that of a confessor and bishop. Ibid., in the Commentary.

**Hugh of Portugal**, bishop and one of the authors of the History of Compostela, used Dexter’s Chronicle and cites certain words from it. In the Eulogies and Part I of the Apology, § 1.

**Hymn on Saint Torquatus and his companions.** Commentary, A.C. 43.

On Saint Crispinus, bishop. Commentary, A.C. 66, no. 5.

On Saint Theodore of Caesaraugusta and his companions. Commentary, A.C. 71, no. 5.

On Saint Eugenius, bishop of Toledo and martyr. Commentary, A.C. 130, no. 3.

On the eight holy sisters. Commentary, A.C. 138, no. 5.

On Saint Marciana, virgin. Commentary, A.C. 155.

On Saint Thyrsus. Commentary, A.C. 286, no. 2.

On Saint Faustus and his companions. Commentary, A.C. 299, at the end.

On Saint Cucuphas. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 21.

On Saints Justa and Regina. Ibid., no. 27.

On Saint Encratis, or Engratia. Ibid., no. 29.

On the eighteen saints of Caesaraugusta. Ibid.

On Saint Vincent. Ibid., no. 30.

On Saint Leocadia. Ibid., no. 31.

On both Eulalias. Ibid., in the Appendix.

On Saints Vincent and his sisters. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 54.

On Saint Zoilus. Ibid., no. 57.

On Saints Justus and Pastor, boys. Commentary, A.C. 423, no. 8.

## I

**Ibineus**, martyr of Ágreda. See the martyrs of Ágreda.

**Idacius of Emerita** persecutes Priscillianus. Dexter, A.C. 384.

**Idacius**, bishop of Braga, takes part in the Council of Caesaraugusta. Ibid., no. 7.

**Idacius**, a distinguished Spaniard: how great a man was he? Commentary, A.C. 384, no. 5. See Dexter, A.C. 429.

**Ignatius** burns with desire to see the Blessed Mary. Commentary, A.C. 35. His letters to her. Dexter, A.C. 116. Their authenticity. In the Commentary. And the Virgin’s letter to him. Ibid. Who accompanied him to Rome as he hastened toward martyrdom? Dexter, A.C. 70; Commentary, no. 5.

[Col. 1252] **Herod and Herodias died miserably at Lérida.** See Herod.

**Licerius**, bishop of Lérida. Dexter, A.C. 268.

**What is the old Spanish word “Ili”?** Commentary, A.C. 54, no. 10.

**Iliturgi**, which city was it? Commentary, A.C. 54, no. 8. Its martyrs. Dexter, A.C. 60. Its presbyter Maurus took part in the Council of Illiberis. Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 5.

**Illiberis**, what city was it formerly? By whom was it founded? From where did its name come? Commentary, A.C. 54, no. 6. Many disciples of Saint James suffered there. Dexter, A.C. 57. Other martyrs of the same place. Dexter, A.C. 60.

**The Council of Illiberis.** Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 5. In what year did it take place? This is treated at length in the Commentary. It was the oldest of all councils whose acts survive. Ibid. Which Fathers took part in it? Ibid. A synod was convened at Toledo in its defense. Dexter, A.C. 311, and the Commentary, where its acts and authority are defended at length. Who compiled its acts? See Hosius and Felix. There was another Council of Illiberis celebrated by the disciples of Saint James. Dexter, A.C. 60.

**Illici and the Gulf of Illici:** where were they? Commentary, A.C. 52, no. 1.

**The Synod of Illici.** Dexter, A.C. 360.

**Ilipula**, which city was it, and how many formerly bore that name? Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 33. The martyrs of Ilipula. Ibid., and Commentary, A.C. 57, no. 1.

**Mount Ilipula.** See Mount Granada.

**Ilorci**, which city was it? Commentary, A.C. 406, no. 2. Its martyr. Ibid., with Dexter.

**Image of the Mother of God**, left by her own hand at Caesaraugusta upon a pillar. Dexter, A.C. 41; Commentary, no. 1.

**Images brought to Spain by Saint Peter.** Dexter, A.C. 50, no. 2. Their widespread use. Dexter, A.C. 208.

**Why were images at one time forbidden by the Council of Illiberis to be painted on church walls?** Commentary, A.C. 311.

**The image of Saint Christopher**, of gigantic stature: since what time has it existed in Spain? Dexter, A.C. 208.

**How Dexter summarized the successions of emperors and supreme pontiffs.** Part I of the Apology, § 2.

**Indalecius**, a disciple and doorkeeper of Saint James, but made a bishop by Saint Peter and sent back to Spain. Commentary, A.C. 37, no. 8, and Dexter, A.C. 43 and 44. Where did he preach? Dexter, A.C. 54. He had formerly been sent by the Spaniards to Peter, and for what reason? Commentary, A.C. 35, no. 7.

**Pope Innocent** writes to the Synod of Toledo. Commentary, A.C. 386, no. 1, and Dexter, A.C. 405. He begins his pontificate. Dexter, A.C. 401.

**The remarkable conversion of Innocentius, a Spanish Jew.** Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 424, no. 11.

**Countless martyrs of Caesaraugusta.** Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, nos. 49, 50, and 51.

**Interamnis**, a Spanish city: which city was it, and how many cities bore that name? Its martyrs. Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 160, no. 2, and A.C. 175.

**The feast of the Invention of the Holy Cross**, instituted by Saint Sylvester. Dexter, A.C. 424.

**Irenaeus**, archdeacon of Caesaraugusta, suffers martyrdom with his companions. Dexter, A.C. 71.

**Irenaeus of Lyon**, bishop, flourishes. Dexter, A.C. 182. To whom did he dedicate his books? Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 182, no. 5.

**The body of Saint James was brought to Iria Flavia.** See James son of Zebedee.

**The Church of Iria**, erected by Saint Peter of Braga. Commentary, A.C. 36, no. 2.

**Martyrs of Iria.** Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, nos. 15 and 21. See Commentary, A.C. 42, no. 3.

**Isacius**, martyr of Alba, with his companions. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 55.

**Isaiah’s prophecy concerning Saint James’s preaching in Spain.** Commentary, A.C. 66, no. 21. [Col. 1253]

**Iscius**, a disciple and reader of Saint James, made a bishop by Saint Peter and sent to Spain. Commentary, A.C. 37, and Dexter, A.C. 43 and 44. Where did he preach? Dexter, A.C. 52. He suffers martyrdom. Dexter, A.C. 57. The discovery of his relics. Ibid., in the Commentary.

**Isicius**, bishop of Toledo. Dexter, A.C. 428 and 429.

**Isidore the Elder of Córdoba**, continuator of Jerome’s Chronicles. Dexter, A.C. 384.

**Four writers named Isidore in Spain.** Commentary, ibid.

**Isidore the Younger of Córdoba** wrote the books of Allegories attributed to Isidore of Seville. Dexter and Commentary, A.C. 423, no. 5, and A.C. 430, no. 11.

**Eulogy of Isidore the Farmer of Madrid.** Commentary, A.C. 248.

**Ispalis**, a city at the foot of the Pyrenees, distinct from Baetican Hispalis. Dexter, A.C. 308; Commentary, no. 16. Its martyrs. Ibid.

**Istonium**, a city of Carpetania. Dexter, A.C. 300; Commentary, no. 6. Its martyrs. Ibid.

**The Italic legion**, which was in Palestine at the time of the death of Christ the Lord, consisted of Spanish soldiers. Commentary, A.C. 54, no. 3.

**Martyrs of Italica.** Commentary, A.C. 60, no. 1, and Dexter, A.C. 100.

**Was the Emperor Theodosius born at Italica or at Cauca in Spain?** Commentary, A.C. 382, no. 4.

**Iturissa**, which city was it? Commentary, A.C. 300, no. 45. Its martyrs. Ibid.

**Izates**, ruler of the Adiabenians, was a Christian. Commentary, A.C. 66, no. 12.

## J
James son of Alphaeus the Apostle: when was he elected bishop of Jerusalem? Dex. and Com. A.D. 34. He suffers martyrdom. Dex. A.D. 61.

James son of Zebedee receives Spain as his lot for preaching. Dex. and Com. A.D. 34. His arrival in Spain is discussed at length. Dex. and Com. A.D. 36 and 37. How many doctors, and which ones, affirm this? Ibid. What Baronius formerly devised in opposition is worthless. Ibid. He establishes many churches there; he preaches to Jews and Gentiles alike, brings many of both groups to the faith, and performs many great miracles there. Ibid. He raises a certain ancient prophet from the dead. Ibid. He organizes the churches of Spain. Ibid. He gives them the liturgy of the Mass. Ibid. He erects the church of Saint Mary of the Pillar at Caesaraugusta, instructed by the Blessed Virgin while she was present. Dex. and Com. A.D. 37. He also dedicates another little shrine to the same Virgin at Bracara. See Hugh of Portugal in the *Elogia*. He writes a canonical epistle in Spain. Dex. and Com. A.D. 37, no. 6. In what year? Dex. A.D. 41. He preaches to the twelve tribes that were in the Dispersion. Ibid. He establishes twelve bishops in Spain—which ones, and where? Com. A.D. 37, no. 8, together with Dextrus. He entrusts the care of the Church of the Pillar to Theodore. Dex. A.D. 41. He leaves Spain and preaches elsewhere. Ibid. He returns to Jerusalem. Ibid. He accompanies the Mother of God when she goes to Ephesus. Ibid.; Com. no. 5. He introduced into Spain the feast of her Conception. Com. A.D. 308, no. 9. He is crowned with martyrdom—in what year? Dex. A.D. 42, and at length in Com. His translation. Ibid. no. 4. Discovery of his relics. Ibid. His preaching in Spain was foretold by Isaiah. Com. A.D. 66, no. 21. His memory has always been celebrated throughout Spain. Dex. A.D. 91.

[Col. 1253] Januarius, martyr of Heraclea, companion of Saint Felix. Dex. A.D. 296. Januarius, martyr with his companions Faustus and Martialis. Ibid., at the end. Januarius, bishop of Calabria, attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5. Januarius, martyr of Ebura, with his companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 20. Januarius, martyr of Caesaraugusta, one of the eighteen companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 50.

Joachim the abbot is expressly defended; he was a Cistercian monk and foresaw the condemnation of his book. Second part of the *Apology*.

John the Apostle is carried alive by angelic hands to Caesaraugusta together with the Blessed Virgin. Dex. A.D. 37; Com. no. 11. He goes with her to Ephesus. Dex. A.D. 41; Com. no. 8. His prophecy concerning the false prophet Muhammad, interpreted by Saint Caecilius. Com. A.D. 54, no. 9. He preaches in Spain. Dex. A.D. 70; Com. no. 5. He is recalled from exile. Dex. A.D. 91. In what year? Ibid. in Com. He writes to Drusia, an elect woman. Dex. A.D. 105.

John of Cluny, martyr with his companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 63.

John of Vergara, a canon of Toledo, had Dextrus’s Chronicle in his possession. First part of the *Apology*, § 1.

The prophet Jonah: where did he wish to go? Com. A.D. 66, no. 22.

Jonah, disciple of Saint Dionysius: where did he preach? Dex. A.D. 86 and A.D. 130. He visits Saint Eugenius at Toledo. Dex. A.D. 112.

Joseph of Arimathea’s exile. Dex. and Com. A.D. 48.

Jovianus, father of monks. Dex. A.D. 424.

Jovianus, the Catholic emperor. Dex. A.D. 364.

The revolt of Judas the Galilaean. Dex. A.D. 2, and Com. ibid.

Judas the Apostle sets out to preach. Dex. and Com. A.D. 41. He goes with Peter to Spain. Dex. A.D. 50. His testimony is explained. First part of the *Apology*, § 2.

Jews. See Hebrews.

The revolt of the Jews in Libya. Dex. A.D. 116. They are dispersed by Hadrian. Dex. A.D. 121. Their revolt in Palestine. Dex. A.D. 135.

The remarkable conversion of the people of Ebura to the faith. Dex. and Com. A.D. 424, no. 11.

Julia, virgin and martyr of Emerita, companion of Saint Eulalia. Com. A.D. 300, at the end.

Julia of Olyssippo, martyr with her brothers. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 11.

Julia of Sentica, martyr. Dex. A.D. 356.

Julia of Myrtilis: which city? See Myrtilis.

Julian, archpriest of Toledo of Saint Justa, used Dextrus’s Chronicle. First part of the *Apology*, § 1, and in the *Elogia*.

Julian, disciple of Saint Peter. Dex. A.D. 86. He is bishop of Carpetania and suffers martyrdom. Dex. A.D. 91 and A.D. 94.

Julian, martyr of Aquis-Quintiana. Dex. A.D. 95.

Julian, martyr of Carthage, companion of Modestus. Com. A.D. 160, no. 1.

Julian, jurist and emperor. Dex. A.D. 195.

Julian, a young man and martyr of Flaviobriga. Dex. A.D. 270. His acts are in Com.

Julian of Tucci, martyr with his companions. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 17.

Julian the Apostate, emperor. Dex. A.D. [Col. 1254] 364. Many write against him. Dex. A.D. 368.

Juliobriga: which city? Com. A.D. 300, no. 19. Its church was established by Saint James, with Saint Arcadius appointed its first bishop. Dex. and Com. A.D. 37, no. 8. Lucia, martyr. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 19.

The port of Juliobriga: which one? Com. A.D. 308, no. 20. Its martyrs. Ibid.

Julitta, martyr with her son Quiricus. Dex. A.D. 222. Their discovery. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 6.

Julius of Abula, to whom Saint Clement wrote. Dex. A.D. 94.

Julius, martyr of Dorostorum. Com. A.D. 168.

Julius Ioschus, a Spanish soldier of the Legion Fulminata. Com. A.D. 175, no. 3.

Julius, Roman pontiff. Dex. A.D. 335.

Julius, martyr of Tarragona with his companions. Com. A.D. 360, no. 4.

Justa and Rufina, virgins and martyrs of Hispalis. Com. A.D. 286, at the end, and Com. A.D. 300, no. 48.

Justina, virgin and martyr of Carmonia. Dex. A.D. 285.

Justin, philosopher and martyr, presents a book on behalf of the religion to the emperor Antoninus. Dex. A.D. 143.

Justus of Hispalis, martyr with his companions Macarius and Rufinus; they are entirely different from Justa and Rufina. Dex. and Com. A.D. 115, no. 1.

Justus and Pastor, child martyrs of Complutum. Dex. A.D. 296. Their father Vitalis, martyr. Dex. A.D. 290. Discovery of their relics. Dex. A.D. 423. See also Dex. A.D. 424, and under Celsus.

Justus, bishop of Vico, renowned for holiness. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 8.

Juvencus, priest and distinguished poet, attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5. What does he write about the peace granted by Constantine to the churches in his time? Com. A.D. 312. He died at Salamanca. Dex. A.D. 337. Concerning him again: Dex. A.D. 407.

# L

Lacobriga: which city? Com. A.D. 120.

Laconimurgum: which city? Dex. and Com. A.D. 120. From there came Diocles, the celebrated charioteer. Ibid.

Lactantius Firmianus: where was he from? Dex. A.D. 317.

Laeda of Barcelona, senator and martyr with her companions. Dex. A.D. 138.

Laetus, martyr of Toledo with his brother Vincentius. Dex. A.D. 352. Their church. Dex. A.D. 353. See the Letter of Silo.

Lalaetania: which province? Com., dedicatory epistle to Orosius, § “To you, a man of Lalaetania.”

Severus, bishop of Lamacitanum, a distinguished writer. Dex. and Com. A.D. 388, no. 5.

Lambertus, martyr of Caesaraugusta, who carried his severed head in his hands. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 14.

The tablets of Mount Grannata. Com. A.D. 57. See Grannata and Mount Grannatensis.

Laminium: which city? Whom did the Apostle Paul convert to the faith there? Dex. and Com. A.D. 64, no. 5.

Lampadius, formerly prefect of the City, becomes bishop of Oretum. Dex. A.D. 282.

Lampadius, or Lampius, bishop of Barcelona, ordains Saint Paulinus priest. Dex. A.D. 396.

Lamponius, priest of Calduba, attended [Col. 1255] the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5.

Largus, martyr of Augustobriga with his companions. Dex. and Com. A.D. 300, no. 22.

Latinus Pacatus delivered a panegyric to Theodosius the Great. Com. A.D. 382, no. 10.

Saint Laurence, a Spanish martyr. Com. A.D. 246. His parents were martyrs, and his homeland is given. Dex. Ibid. He suffers martyrdom. Dex. A.D. 260, and Com. no. 4.

Laurence de Padilla, Caesarean historiographer, used Dextrus’s Chronicle in many places. First part of the *Apology*, § 1.

Laureolus was acted by Lentulus in mockery of the Christians. Dex. A.D. 86. Who he was. Com. ibid.

Laurus: the city whose priest Januarius attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5.

Lazarus accompanies the Blessed Virgin when she goes to Ephesus. Dex. and Com. A.D. 41. He is sent into exile and becomes bishop of Massilia. Com. A.D. 48.

Lazarus, bishop of Vico, sends Orosius to Augustine. Dex. and Com. A.D. 400.

The martyrs of León. Com. A.D. 298. Their bishop Decentius attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5.

Leo, priest of Accinippo, attended the Council of Illiberis. Ibid.

Leo, priest of Augusta Gemella, was likewise present. Ibid.

Leocadia, virgin and martyr of Toledo. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 52. Her acts are in Com. Her church. Com. A.D. 312.

Leonas, bishop of Lugo. Com. A.D. 385, no. 2.

Leontius, a Spanish bishop to whom Saint Melchiades wrote. Com. A.D. 299, no. 3.

Marcus Aurelius exhibited one hundred lions to the Roman people. Dex. A.D. 182.

Leonides, martyr and father of Origen. Dex. A.D. 204.

Leovigild, king of the Goths: in what respect was he the eleventh horn of Daniel’s fourth beast? Appendix to A.D. 430.

The lapse and repentance of Leporius, bishop of Utica in Baetica; he was a disciple of Saint Augustine. Dex. and Com. A.D. 406, no. 1. See the second part of the *Apology*, at the end of this work, against G. Pennotus.

There was only one Leporius, not two. Ibid.

Lero, the island to which Hyginus of Corduba was taken: what sort of place was it? Com. A.D. 384, no. 9, and second part of the *Apology*.

The river Lethe: where is it? Dex. A.D. 208. There are many of this name. Ibid. in Com. no. 8.

Liberata, virgin and sister of eight other martyrs, otherwise called Wilgefortis. Dex. and Com. A.D. 138, no. 6. Her acts are in Com. See Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 3.

Liberatus, bishop of Illiberis. Dex. A.D. 66; Com. no. 20.

Liberatus, priest of Eliocroca, attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5.

Liberius, father of Saint Eulalia of Emerita. Com. A.D. 300, no. 52, in her acts.

Pope Liberius. Dex. A.D. 353. Dextrus rightly calls him a saint. Ibid. in Com.

Libora: which city? Com. A.D. 130, no. 6.

Many books, at the time of the Saracen disaster, were brought from Spain into Germany. First part of the *Apology*, § 1.

The books of Mount Saint Grannatensis. Com. A.D. 37, no. 2; and at great length Com. A.D. 54, where the book of Saint Caecilius, written in the Spanish language, is discussed. They lend credibility to Dextrus. Com. A.D. 57. What do they say about the Conception of the Virgin? Com. A.D. 308, no. 9.

The book *On the Birth and Death of the Fathers* was truly written by Isidore of Hispalis. Com. A.D. 37, no. 6.

Who first wrote the *Book of the Births of the Martyrs*? Dex. A.D. 324; Com. no. 2.

To whom did Dionysius dedicate his books? To whom did Irenaeus? See Dionysius and Irenaeus.

Licerius, bishop of Ilerda. Dex. A.D. 268 and Com. no. 8. He transfers the see of Carense to Ilerda. Dex. A.D. 311.

The pontificate of Pope Linus. Dex. A.D. 69.

The letters of Hosius to the emperor Constantius, full of Christian liberty. Com. A.D. 356, no. 1.

Loaysa, bishop of Toledo, wrongly multiplies the Councils of Caesaraugusta. Com. A.D. 284, no. 7.

Luke was present at Paul’s martyrdom. Com. A.D. 66, no. 16.

Luke, martyr of Hispalis with his companions. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 16.

The death of the poet Lucan. Dex. A.D. 66.

The church of Lugo was established by Saint James, with Saint Capito appointed its first bishop. Dex. and Com. A.D. 37, no. 8.

Saint Forcatus, bishop of Lugo. Dex. A.D. 385.

Lucia of Macedonia, martyr. Dex. A.D. 100; Com. no. 17. She is the same as Lydia the Purple-Dyer. Ibid. in Com.

Lucia, virgin and martyr of Juliobriga. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 19.

Lucia, martyr of Heraclea. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 35.

Lucian, bishop of Beauvais, is transferred to Vico. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 8.

Lucian, bishop of Caesaraugusta and writer. Dex. A.D. 430.

Luciolus, martyr of Ebura with his companions. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 20.

Lucius. See below.

Lucius, martyr and husband of Saint Candida. Dex. A.D. 100; Com. no. 19.

Lucius, emperor. Dex. A.D. 165 to 172.

Lucius the Spaniard flourishes at Rome. Dex. A.D. 180.

Lucius, bishop of Barcelona. Dex. A.D. 208.

Pope Lucius. Dex. A.D. 256.

Lucius Valerius. See Valerius.

Lucretia, virgin and martyr of Emerita. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 22.

Luparia Regula of Gallaecia is converted to the faith. Com. A.D. 42, no. 3.

Luparia of Baetica, daughter of another Luparia of Acci, converted to the faith. Com. A.D. 43, no. 1. Concerning her: Dex. A.D. 60; Com. no. 5.

Luparius, disciple of Saint Thesiphontus, martyr of Grannata. Com. A.D. 57.

Lupercus, or Lupercius, martyr of Caesaraugusta, one of the eighteen companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 50.

Lupercius, martyr of León with his brothers. Com. A.D. 298.

Lupus, martyr. See Marcus Lupus.

Lupus, martyr of Deobriga with his companion. Dex. A.D. 285.

Lupus, bishop of Tela, attended the Council of Caesaraugusta. Dex. A.D. 384.

Martyrs of Lusitania under Nero. Dex. A.D. 60.

Luxurius, priest of Drona, attended [Col. 1256] the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 500, no. 5.

Lybisosa: which city? Com. A.D. 64, no. 5. A church of Saints Vincentius and Laetus was erected there. Dex. A.D. 353.

Lydia the Purple-Dyer. See Lucia of Macedonia.

# M

Macedon of Barcelona, martyr. Com. A.D. 138, no. 2.

Macarius, martyr of Hispalis with his companions. Dex. A.D. 115.

Macrinus, emperor. Dex. A.D. 219.

Mademarius, bishop of Barcelona. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 3.

Magdalene accompanies the Blessed Virgin when she goes to Ephesus. Dex. and Com. A.D. 41. She goes into exile with her companions in Gaul. Dex. A.D. 48. She dies peacefully. Dex. A.D. 88.

Another Magdalene of the same name died in Spain. Com. A.D. 42, no. 4.

The Magi, after worshipping Christ, later suffer for him. Dex. A.D. 70. Their names. Ibid. And their acts. In Com. Where their bodies were located. Ibid.

Maginus, martyr of Tarragona. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 18.

Majorianus, bishop of Toledo. Dex. A.D. 429. He is entirely different from Martinus, or Marinus. Ibid. in Com. no. 2.

Patricius, bishop of Malaga, attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5.

Felicianus, bishop and martyr. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 14.

The relics of Saint Mammantis were brought to Gallaecia. Dex. A.D. 430. His memory is preserved on Mount Saint Mammetis, which belongs to the Monastery of the Mount of Branches. Ibid. in Com. no. 3.

Mancius, a disciple of Christ and bishop of Ebura. Dex. A.D. 90. He preaches in Gaul. Ibid. He is the same as Memmius, bishop of Châlons. Com. ibid., and Dex. A.D. 430.

The origin of the Manichaeans. Dex. A.D. 280.

Mantua of the Carpetani: which city? Com. A.D. 248. Its martyrs. Dex. and Com. A.D. 308, no. 12, and A.D. 353. Saint Melchiades and Saint Damasus, Roman pontiffs, were born there. See under those names. Saint Isidore the Farmer was also born there. See under his name.

Marabaudes the blind, of Barcelona, lyric poet. Dex. A.D. 423.

Marcella, maidservant of Magdalene and Martha, is sent into exile. Dex. and Com. A.D. 48, no. 1.

M. Marcellus. See Eugenius of Toledo.

Marcellus the Roman, martyr and kinsman of Saint Eugenius of Toledo. Dex. A.D. 71.

M. Marcellus, prefect of Rome and quaestor of Hispania Citerior, father of Saint Eugenius. Dex. A.D. 100.

Marcellus, nephew of Saint Eugenius through his brother. Dex. A.D. 110.

Marcellus, martyr of León. Com. A.D. 268, no. 9. His sons. Com. A.D. 298, where he is discussed again. See also under Marinus the Spaniard.

Marcellus of Solia, martyr and bishop in Baetica. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 28.

Marcellus of Cluny, martyr with his companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 63.

Marcellus, bishop of Castulo, takes part in the Council of Corduba. Dex. A.D. 356.

Marcellus, bishop of Tela. Dex. A.D. 382.

Marcellus, bishop of Coria, expels the Priscillianists from the city. Dex. A.D. 424.

[Col. 1257] Marcellinus of Cluny, martyr with his companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 63.

Marcia, martyr of Ebura with her companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 20.

Marciana, virgin and martyr: there are two of this name, with their acts. Com. A.D. 138, no. 5, and Dex. A.D. 155.

Marciana of Cluny, martyr with her companions. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 63.

Martialis, bishop of Toulouse, visits Spain. Dex. A.D. 52.

Martialis the poet of Bilbilis criticizes the martyrs. Dex. A.D. 60; Com. no. 7.

Martialis, bishop of Emerita, deposed. Com. A.D. 255, no. 2.

Martialis, martyr and companion of Saints Justus and Januarius. Com. A.D. 299, at the end.

Martialis of Caesaraugusta, martyr, one of the eighteen companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 50.

Marcus Marcellus Eugenius. See Eugenius of Toledo.

Marcus, martyr of Castulo. Dex. and Com. A.D. 66.

Marcus Mancinus, duumvir of Barcelona. Dex. A.D. 91.

Marcellus, prefect of Rome and father of Saint Eugenius. See Marcellus.

Marcus Lupus, martyr. Dex. A.D. 100; Com. no. 19.

Marcus Bolanus. See Florentius of Hispalis.

Marcus, first patriarch of Jerusalem from among the Gentiles. Dex. A.D. 138.

Marcus, a Gnostic heretic, visits Spain; his acts. Dex. and Com. A.D. 169. He is expelled from Toledo and Valencia. Ibid.

Marcus Aurelius Verus, prefect of Spain and persecutor of the Christians. Dex. and Com. A.D. 300, no. 14.

Marcus, martyr of Caparra with his companions. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 19.

Marcus, Roman pontiff. Dex. A.D. 335.

Marcus, lyric poet of Corcheium. Dex. A.D. 368. Perhaps Matronianus.

Margarita. See Marina.

MARY, Mother of God: in what manner was she the head of the apostles while still living? Dex. and Com. A.D. 34, no. 10. During her lifetime she was visited by believers flocking to her from everywhere. Dex. A.D. 25. She appears to Saint James at Caesaraugusta and orders him to erect a church for her. Dex. and Com. A.D. 37. Her activities after the Son’s Ascension. Ibid. no. 12. It is demonstrated that she lived for some time at Caesaraugusta. Com. A.D. 38, no. 1. In what year was she assumed to the Son? This is discussed at length. Com. A.D. 48, no. 1.

Mary Magdalene. See Magdalene.

Mary of Clopas travels through Spain. Com. A.D. 42, no. 4.

Mary Salome travels in Spain and dies at Veroli in Italy. Com. A.D. 42, no. 4.

Mary, virgin and martyr of Veroviscum, surnamed Ancilla. Dex. A.D. 360.

Maria, wife of the emperor Honorius, a Spaniard. Com. A.D. 388, no. 9.

Marianus, martyr of Flaviobriga with his companions. Com. A.D. 182, no. 3.

Marina, virgin, otherwise Gemma-Marina. Dex. A.D. 138. She is the same as Margarita, who is wrongly thought to be Greek. Com. at length. Discovery of her body. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 7.

Marinus the Spaniard, martyr. Dex. A.D. 268; Com. no. 9.

Marinus the Spaniard, bishop to whom Saint Melchiades wrote. Com. A.D. 299, no. 3.

Maronius, disciple of Saint Iscius, martyr of Grannata. Com. A.D. 57.

[Col. 1257] Martha accompanies the Blessed Virgin when she goes to Ephesus. Dex. and Com. A.D. 41. She goes into exile in Gaul. Dex. A.D. 48.

Martha, virgin and martyr of Carthage with her female companions. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 7.

Martinus, bishop of Tours, flourishes. Dex. A.D. 382. He takes part in the Council of Caesaraugusta. Dex. A.D. 384.

Martinus, otherwise Marinus, bishop of Toledo. Dex. A.D. 424.

Martula: which city? Com. A.D. 308, no. 1. Its martyr was Saint Brictius, bishop. Ibid. in Dex.

Martyrs criticized by the poet Martialis. Dex. A.D. 60; Com. no. 7. Those killed at Rome by Nero. Ibid. Those killed in Gaul and Spain in the time of Marcus Aurelius. Dex. and Com. A.D. 170, no. 1. See under Persecution and throughout the Chronicle.

A slight correction is required in the reading of the martyrology. Com. A.D. 70, no. 7; Com. A.D. 71, no. 2; Com. A.D. 95, no. 4; Com. A.D. 100, no. 14; Com. A.D. 112, no. 4; Com. A.D. 138, nos. 2 and 3, and so forth—namely, in Victoria, Quiteria, and Basilla; and Com. A.D. 139, no. 4; Com. A.D. 175, no. 2; Com. A.D. 208, no. 4; Com. A.D. 222, no. 2; Com. A.D. 230, no. 2; Com. A.D. 255, no. 4, under the virgin Anatholia; Com. A.D. 296, no. 2; Com. A.D. 300, nos. 22, 25, and 37; Com. A.D. 300, no. 44; Com. A.D. 308, nos. 14 and 11; Com. A.D. 382, no. 9.

Massia, a city of Spain: how many martyrs did it have, and who were they? Com. A.D. 168.

Lazarus and his sisters are exiled at Massilia. Dex. and Com. A.D. 48, no. 1.

Paulus, bishop of Massifi. Dex. A.D. 418.

Matthias the Apostle sets out to preach. Dex. and Com. A.D. 41. He suffers martyrdom. Dex. and Com. A.D. 66. Where is his body located? Ibid.

Matronianus, a celebrated poet but colleague of Priscillian. Com. A.D. 368, no. 3.

In what year did Matthew write the Gospel? Dex. and Com. A.D. 41. He sets out to preach. Ibid.

Matutinus, martyr of Caesaraugusta, one of the eighteen companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 50.

Maurus, priest of Iliturgi, attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5.

Maxencia of Coria flourishes at Trent. Dex. A.D. 419. She was the mother of Saint Vigilius the bishop. Com. Ibid.

Maxima, virgin of Coria, suffers martyrdom at Rome. Dex. A.D. 360.

Maxima, martyr and wife of the martyr Montanus. Dex. A.D. 100.

Maxima, virgin and martyr of Olyssippo with her brothers. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 11.

Maxentius, the tyrant, defeated by the emperor Constantine. Dex. A.D. 312. See Com.

Maximianus, martyr of Blandae with his companion Bonosus. Dex. A.D. 156.

Maximianus, emperor, defeated by Narseus. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 10. Concerning him: Dex. A.D. 300; Com. nos. 18, 20, and 21.

Maximianus, martyr of Urgabo with his companion. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 4.

Maximianus, confessor and bishop, celebrated at Viana. Dex. A.D. 424.

Maximinus, companion of Magdalene, goes into exile. Dex. and Com. A.D. 48, no. 1.

Maximinus, emperor. Dex. A.D. 238, 239, and 240, in which year he was killed.

Maximus, disciple of Saint James in Spain, ordained priest by him. Com. A.D. 37. He suffers martyrdom. Dex. A.D. 66.

[Col. 1258] Maximus, disciple of Saint Thesiphontus, suffers martyrdom. Com. A.D. 57.

Maximus of Tyre flourishes. Dex. A.D. 149.

Maximus and Dadas, martyrs: where were they killed? Dex. and Com. A.D. 290, no. 2.

Maximus, martyr of Gerunda with his companion. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 43.

The emperor Maximus: by whom was he hailed? He was a tyrant. Dex. A.D. 384. He is killed. Dex. A.D. 388.

Meco, a city devastated by the Goths in Carpetania: which city? Dex. and Com. A.D. 429, no. 10.

Caius, bishop of Milan: who was he? Dex. A.D. 70; Com. no. 5. The council attended by the emperor Theodosius. Dex. A.D. 382. He is defended. Ibid. in Com.

Philippus Philotheus, a citizen of Milan. See under that name.

The bodies of the three Magi were at Milan. Com. A.D. 70, no. 1. Its church was founded by Barnabas. See Barnabas, Ambrose, Gervasius, and Auxentius.

Melantius, bishop of Toledo. Dex. A.D. 286. He attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5. He died. Dex. A.D. 310.

Pope Melchiades, African by origin but born in Spain, at Mantua of the Carpetani. Dex. A.D. 248, and in Com. and Dex. A.D. 299, no. 3. He becomes pontiff. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 25.

Melecius, leader of Cluny, suffered martyrdom with his companions. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 6. Melecion, his companion. Ibid. in Com.

Melecius, a Jew, converted to the faith in a marvelous manner. Com. A.D. 424, no. 11.

Mela: the place-name corrected. Com. A.D. 52, no. 1.

Mellaria, the city and homeland of Pomponius Mela: which city? Com. A.D. 300, no. 14. Firmus, martyr. Ibid. with Dex.

Memmius, bishop of Châlons, the same as Mancius of Ebura. Com. A.D. 90. See Mancius.

The Greek *Menologion* supports the statements of Dextrus. First part of the *Apology*, § 1.

Mercurius of Cluny, martyr with his companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 63.

Mesito, martyr of Grannata. Com. A.D. 57.

The Blessed Virgin gives a letter to the people of Messina. Dex. A.D. 86 and A.D. 430.

Metellinum: which city? Com. A.D. 134, no. 4. Its martyrs. Dex. Ibid. A confessor. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 46.

Metellus of Targe, a writer who spoke intelligently about the division of the provinces among the apostles. Com. A.D. 34, no. 10.

The metropolises of Spain were formerly divided. See Eugenius of Toledo. They were designated again under the emperor Constantine, together with their suffragan sees. Com. A.D. 324, no. 3.

Mevania, or Mevitania: which city, where, and how many bore this name? Dex. and Com. A.D. 100, nos. 21 and 22.

Minervius, father of monks. Dex. A.D. 424.

Minobriga. See Munobriga, otherwise Mirobriga.

The miracles of the Apostle Saint James while preaching in Spain. Dex. and Com. A.D. 37, no. 4. Those of his disciples. Com. A.D. 43, no. 1.

Mirobriga. See Munobriga.

Modestus, martyr of Carthage with his companion. Dex. A.D. 160.

Monks in Spain from the time of Diocletian. Dex. and Com. A.D. 308, no. 6. Black people in Lusitania: when? Dex. A.D. 419.

The monarchy of the Spanish kings: in what did it consist, and when was it founded? Appendix to A.D. 430.

[Col. 1259] The monastery of monks at Titulcia, dedicated to the Blessed Virgin in the time of Diocletian. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 6.

Monica, mother of Augustine. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 37.

The Mozarabic Breviary and Missal contributed greatly to this elucidation. First part of the *Apology*, § 3.

Munda: which city? Com. A.D. 308, no. 24. Its martyr. Ibid. in Dex.

The division of the world among the sons of Noah: what was it? Com. A.D. 66, no. 22.

Munobriga: which city, and how many were there? Com. A.D. 300, no. 23. Its martyr. Dex. Ibid.

Myrtilis, or Julia-Myrtilis: which city? Com. A.D. 308, no. 1.

Mysia is incorrectly read in many places of the martyrology instead of Masia. Com. A.D. 168.

# N

Narcissus, bishop of Bracara. Dex. A.D. 268 and A.D. 277. See also Com., where Narcissus and Felix of Gerunda are discussed at length.

The birthdays of the martyrs: why are their feast days so called? Com. A.D. 324, no. 2.

Natalis, priest of Orsuna, attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5. He becomes bishop of Toledo. Dex. and Com. A.D. 310, no. 3. He attended the Council of Nicaea. Dex. A.D. 324. He celebrates a council at Toledo. Ibid. He sent Constantine a book of the births of the holy martyrs, of which he himself was the author. Ibid. He died. Dex. A.D. 352.

Nathanael, disciple of Christ: where does he rest? Dex. and Com. A.D. 105, no. 5.

The house of the Mother of God at Nazareth is consecrated as a church by the apostles. Dex. A.D. 42; Com. no. 1.

When was the Council of Neocaesarea convened? Dex. A.D. 316.

Nereus, martyr and companion of Saint Achilleus. Dex. A.D. 91.

The affairs of the emperor Nero. Dex. from A.D. 60 onward. His death: in what year? Dex. and Com. A.D. 69.

Nestor, disciple of Saint James, appointed by him the first bishop of Palencia. Dex. and Com. A.D. 37, no. 8. He suffers martyrdom. Dex. A.D. 60.

Nertobriga: which city? Com. A.D. 300, no. 59. Its martyrs. Ibid.

The black color of monks’ clothing: whence did it arise? Com. A.D. 419, no. 3.

Nivaria: where is the city? Dex. and Com. A.D. 208, no. 4. Its martyr Andeolus. Ibid.

Snow falls from heaven upon the body of each of the two Eulalias. Com. A.D. 300, no. 52.

The Council of Nicaea, of 318 Fathers, against Arius: in what year was it convened? Dex. and Com. A.D. 324, no. 1. Whether Hosius presided there in place of Saint Sylvester? Com.

Nizephorus, martyr of Ursaona. Com. A.D. 115, no. 2.

Nonia, martyr, wife of Saint Marcellus of León and mother of the twelve martyrs. Com. A.D. 298.

Nine anonymous martyrs of Ursaona. Com. A.D. 115, no. 2.

Nine anonymous martyrs of Metellinum. Dex. A.D. 134.

The enormous number of people found by Augustus in the census at Rome. Com. A.D. 14.

The daily number of martyrs: how great was it? Com. A.D. 384, no. 3.

Numia-Varia, the very famous priestess of Venus. Dex. and Com. A.D. 255, no. 3.

[Col. 1259] # O

The objections raised against the authenticity of this codex are dissipated. First part of the *Apology*, § 2, and the second part of the *Apology* throughout.

Oceanus, martyr of Hispalis with his companions. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 16.

Oceanus, martyr of Tucci with his companions. Ibid. no. 7.

Octaviola, a city of Vezozabia: which city? Com. A.D. 290, no. 2. Its martyrs. Dex. Ibid.

Eighty-six anonymous martyrs, who suffered at Concordia in Lusitania. Com. A.D. 145, no. 2.

Octogessa: which city? Com. A.D. 94, no. 5. Its martyr. Ibid.

Oenomaus, philosopher. Dex. A.D. 122.

The Olcades: which people? Com. A.D. 100, no. 14, and A.D. 285. Their martyrs are discussed in Dextrus.

An olive tree used to blossom every year beside the tomb of Saint Torquatus. Com. A.D. 66, no. 4.

Oliva: which city? See Juvencus the poet.

The calculation of Olympiads corresponding to the years of the Lord: what was it? Com. A.D. 1, and Com. A.D. 34, no. 1.

Olympius, bishop of Toledo, the first of that name: who was he? Dex. and Com. A.D. 352, no. 1. He was renowned among the doctors of the Church. Ibid., at length. His acts. Dex. A.D. 356. He took part in the Council of Corduba. Ibid.

Olympius II, bishop of Toledo. Dex. A.D. 424. He died renowned for holiness. Ibid.

The martyrs of Olyssippo. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 11. Others also flourished there. Ibid. no. 22.

The omission of important matters in this codex, through the fault of the copyists. First part of the *Apology*, § 3.

What is called a universal history? Dextrus’s Chronicle rightly bears this name. First part of the *Apology*, § 2, and Com., epistle to Orosius, § “Moreover, Universal,” and § “The Universal Chronicle.”

The preaching of Onesimus, a disciple of the apostles, in Spain. Dex. and Com. A.D. 71.

Ophir was in the region of Bracara. Dex. and Com. A.D. 66, no. 22.

Oppius. See Caius Oppius.

Optatus of Caesaraugusta, martyr, one of the eighteen companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 50.

The orarium and ring of the holy martyrs Emeterius and Celedonius flew up to heaven. Com. A.D. 299.

To what extent Boniface was called a member of the Augustinian order. Com. A.D. 429, no. 3.

Orentius, father of Saint Laurence, martyr with his wife. Dex. and Com. A.D. 246.

Orentius, bishop of Auch, brother of Saint Laurence. Ibid.

Oretum: which city, and where? Com. A.D. 300, no. 16. A confessor of Oretum. Ibid. in Dex. A bishop. See Lampadius.

Origen flourishes. Dex. A.D. 211. He went to Caesarea. Dex. A.D. 235. His father was a martyr. See Leonides and Paul Orosius.

Oronius, martyr of Juliobriga with his companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 19.

Orontius, martyr of Pax Augusta with his companion. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 24.

The family of the Orosii: what was it, and from where did it derive its origin? See in the Life of the Author.

Orosius, uncle of Paul Orosius, shines in holiness at Rome. Dex. A.D. 352; Com. no. 2.

Orosius the elder dies at Rome. Dex. A.D. 366.

Orosius, his son, distinct from the writer Paul Orosius. Dex. Ibid. no. 3.

[Col. 1260] The writer Paul Orosius is born. Dex. A.D. 375. He sets out for the African council. Dex. A.D. 400. He begins *Hormestra*. Dex. and Com. A.D. 417.

His statement concerning the Conception of the Virgin: how is it to be understood? Com. A.D. 308, no. 9.

Isidore of Corduba dedicates the books of the *Allegories* to Orosius. Dex. A.D. 423.

Paul Orosius persecuted the Origenists. Com. A.D. 400, no. 2.

Orsuna. See Ursaona.

Ortigius is restored to his see by the Fathers of the Council of Toledo. Com. A.D. 400, no. 1.

Osca: which city? There are two cities of this name, one in Baetica and the other in Celtiberia. Com. A.D. 138, no. 3, and Com. A.D. 246.

The martyrs of Osca. In both places, in Dextrus.

Osius of Corduba. See Hosius.

Ossonoba: which city? Its bishop Vincentius attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5.

When was the entrance of the Gospel opened to the Gentiles? Com. A.D. 36, at length, and Dex. A.D. 40.

The empire of Otho I. Dex. A.D. 70.

Ovantius, martyr of Uxama-Barca. Dex. A.D. 91.

The death of Ovid Naso. Dex. and Com. A.D. 19.

Ovidius, friend of Caeso Maximus: what sort of man was he? Com. A.D. 66, no. 15.

Ovidius, bishop of Bracara. Dex. A.D. 95. Who was he? Com. Ibid. See Dex. A.D. 110.

# P
## P

Pacianus, bishop of Barcelona, father of Dexter. Dex. and Com. A.D. 375, no. 2, and A.D. 396, no. 1. See the Life of the Author.

Palmo, a city—which one? Com. A.D. 300, no. 37. There Saint Soter, a Roman virgin, suffered martyrdom. Dex. ibid.

Palemon the rhetorician. Dex. A.D. 135.

The Church of Palencia, established by Saint James, with Saint Nestor appointed there as its first bishop. Dex. and Com. A.D. 37, no. 8. See Tela, Pamea, and Antoninus the martyr.

The boundaries of Palestine—which were they? Com. A.D. 66, no. 22.

Palladia of Cluny, martyr, with her companions. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 63.

Palmasius, bishop of Toledo, writes against Vigilantius. Com. A.D. 388, no. 11, at the end.

Pamea, a city—which one, and how many cities bore that name? Com. A.D. 308, no. 21. Its martyr. Ibid., in Dexter.

Pantenus, a Christian philosopher. Dex. A.D. 197.

The Pantheon at Rome—by whom was it constructed? Com. A.D. 86, no. 4. Struck by lightning. Dex. A.D. 112.

Panuntius, disciple of Saint Iscius, martyr. Com. A.D. 57.

Papianus, martyr of Juliobriga, with his companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 19.

Papius, martyr of Segisamo. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 64.

The relics of Parmena and his companions brought from Persia to Córdoba. Dex. ibid., no. 1.

The birth of many children at once. Com. A.D. 138, no. 6.

A serious controversy arose concerning Easter under Pope Victor. Dex. A.D. 199.

Paschasius, martyr of Salamanca, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 430.

Pastor and Justus, boys and martyrs of Complutum. Dex. A.D. 296. Discovery of their relics. Dex. A.D. 423. See under the entries Asturius, Hymnus, and Celsus.

The shepherds who worshiped Christ newly born: how many were there, and what kind? Dex. and Com. A.D. [year not supplied], no. 3. [Col. 1261]

Pasycrates, a man remarkable for holiness. Dex. A.D. 168. He lived not in Thrace but in Spain. Com. ibid. Where his companions are discussed.

Patavonium, a city—which one? Com. A.D. 300, no. 18. Its martyrs. Dex. ibid.

Paternus, a citizen of Toledo, is converted through the preaching of Saint Saturninus. Dex. A.D. 76. He preaches to the people of Bilbilis. Dex. A.D. 94. He flourishes. Dex. A.D. 112. His deeds and martyrdom. Dex. A.D. 130.

Paternus, bishop of Braga: in what did he err? He presides over the Council of Toledo. Com. A.D. 386, no. 1. He was not a prelate of Toledo, as Loaysa thought. Ibid. and Dex. A.D. 407.

Patientia, mother of Saint Lawrence, killed for Christ together with her husband. Dex. A.D. 246.

The fathers of the Council of Zaragoza who condemned Priscillian. Com. A.D. 384, no. 7.

The fathers of the Council of Toledo. Com. A.D. 400, no. 1.

The fathers of the Council of Braga. Com. A.D. 423, no. 6.

The fathers of the Council of Iliberris. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5.

“Patriarch” means the same as “primate.” Com. A.D. 105, no. 6.

Patricius, disciple of Saint Caecilius, suffered martyrdom with him. Com. A.D. 57.

Patricius of Málaga, bishop, attended the Council of Iliberris. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5.

Patruinus, bishop of Toledo. Dex. A.D. 160, and A.D. 208, no. 6.

Paula, virgin and martyr of Carthage, with her companions. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 5.

Paulatus. See Pomponius Paulatus.

Paulillus, a boy of Salamanca, companion of the martyrs. Dex. A.D. 430.

Paulinus of Nola becomes a presbyter at Barcelona. Dex. A.D. 396. His acts and writings, his wife and son. Com. ibid. See Celsus and Tarasia.

Paulinus, governor of the city of Tarragona. Com. A.D. 396, no. 1. Others of that name in Spain. Ibid.

The apostle Paul is converted to the faith—which year? Dex. A.D. 38, with Com. no. 1. In what year did he go up to Jerusalem after his conversion? Ibid. He succeeds James and undertakes his preaching. Com. A.D. 36. He ardently desires to go to Spain rather than to Rome. Ibid. He preaches in Spain and brings many disciples with him. Dex. and Com. A.D. 64. His deeds. Ibid. To which Hebrews did he write? Dex. and Com. A.D. 66. He returns to Rome. Dex. ibid. In what year did he suffer martyrdom? Com. A.D. 68. His arrival in Spain is demonstrated at length. Com. A.D. 64, no. 4.

Paul of Narbonne, bishop, preaches in Spain. Dex. and Com. A.D. 66. Who he was. Ibid. He preaches there again, and in which cities. Dex. A.D. 76.

Paul Orosius. See Orosius.

Paul of Concordia, a very old presbyter, to whom Jerome writes. Dex. A.D. 418.

Paul, bishop of Tarragona—which Paul? Com. A.D. 429, no. 3.

Pax Augusta—which city? Com. A.D. 64, no. 6. Its martyrs. Ibid., and Dex. A.D. 308, Com. no. 24.

Pelagia, martyr of Tarragona, with her companions. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 10.

Pelagius, a citizen of Toledo, is converted through the preaching of Saint Saturninus. Dex. A.D. 76. He becomes bishop of Toledo. Dex. A.D. 138. [Col. 1261]

Pelagius, bishop of Oviedo, a celebrated writer. First part, Apology, § 1. He agrees with Dexter when discussing the disciples of Saint James. Com. A.D. 36 and 37.

Peninsula, a city of Spain, formerly called by the Greeks Cherronesus, now Peñíscola. Com. A.D. 60, no. 2.

The pilgrimage of the faithful to Blessed Mary, still living in the flesh. Dex. A.D. 35. How ancient was the pilgrimage to the holy places of Spain? Dex. A.D. 70; Com. no. 2.

Peregrinus the philosopher throws himself upon the fire at Pisa. Dex. A.D. 167.

The first persecution after the death of Saint Stephen. Dex. A.D. 35. Many of the refugees then came to Spain. Ibid.

When did Nero’s persecution begin in Spain? Dex. A.D. 60.

Under Domitian. Dex. A.D. 86.

Under Trajan. Com. A.D. 100, no. 13.

Under Marcus Aurelius. Com. A.D. 170.

Under Severus. Com. A.D. 204.

Under Maximinus. Com. A.D. 239.

Under Decius. Dex. A.D. 252.

The same under Valerian. Com. A.D. 268, nos. 1 and 2.

Under Diocletian. Dex. A.D. 286.

Perseveranda, virgin of Caracena. Dex. A.D. 360.

The death of the poet Persius. Dex. and Com. A.D. 66.

Pertinax, emperor. Dex. A.D. 195.

A famous pestilence. Dex. A.D. 175. Another. Dex. A.D. 255.

Petronilla, a virgin and daughter born in marriage to the apostle Saint Peter. Dex. A.D. 34; Com. no. 4.

Peter the apostle preaches in Spain, Africa, and Egypt. Dex. A.D. 50, with Com. His journeys. Ibid. He returns to Rome. Dex. A.D. 66; Com. no. 21. In what year did he suffer martyrdom? Dex. and Com. A.D. 68.

Peter of Braga is raised from the dead by Blessed James. Com. A.D. 37, no. 2. He was the first bishop of Braga. Ibid. and no. 8, with Dexter. His death and reputation. Dex. and Com. A.D. 66. He shines through miracles. Dex. A.D. 110. Also concerning him. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 1. His relics preserved. Com. A.D. 423, no. 6, chapter 3 of the Acts of the Council of Braga.

Peter-Megistos—which Peter? Dex. A.D. 66; Com. no. 16.

Peter of Zaragoza, an orator and public grammarian. Com. A.D. 360, at the end.

Peter, a presbyter of Toledo, is celebrated in Africa. Dex. A.D. 424. He dies at Zaragoza. Ibid., no. 13.

Phegadius, bishop of Agen, presided over the Councils of Zaragoza and Valencia. Dex. A.D. 384, and Com. no. 7.

Philemon comes to Spain with Paul. Dex. A.D. 64. He preaches. Ibid. Com. A.D. 47.

Philemon of Carthage, martyr, with a companion. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 24.

Philetus, disciple of Saint James. Com. A.D. 42. He suffers at Old Carthage, which lay between Tarragona and Lérida. Ibid.

Philetus, a senator of Barcelona, martyr with his companions. Dex. A.D. 138.

Philippa of Huesca, martyr. Dex. A.D. 138.

Philip the apostle sets out to preach. Dex. and Com. A.D. 41.

Philip Philothen, a citizen of Milan, converted by Paul in Spain. Dex. A.D. 64. Concerning him. Dex. A.D. 91. He preaches at Barcelona and elsewhere. Ibid. His deeds. Com. A.D. 91, no. 6, and A.D. 105, no. 6.

Philip, emperor. Dex. A.D. 244. He rules together with his son Philip. Com. ibid. They celebrate the thousandth year from the founding of the City. They were the first Christian emperors. Com. A.D. 249. They are killed. Com. A.D. 252, no. 1. [Col. 1262]

Philip of Toledo, disciple of Saint Jerome. Dex. A.D. 429.

Philibertus, abbot and martyr, with a companion, at Titulcia. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 6.

Photina. See the Samaritan woman.

Pilate is sent as procurator to Judaea. Dex. A.D. 28, with Com. His wife believes in Christ. Dex. and Com. A.D. 34, no. 2. He writes to Tiberius Caesar about Christ’s miracles. Com. A.D. 34, and Dex. A.D. 38. His bitter death. Ibid. The lineage of the Pilates still survives. Ibid.

Pidna, a city—also called Piocium—which one? Com. A.D. 95, no. 1. Its martyr. Dex. ibid.

Pimenius of Aix, martyr. Dex. A.D. 130.

Pimenius, bishop of Dumium, confessor. Ibid., in Com.

Piocium. See Pidna.

Pionius, martyr in Asia. Dex. A.D. 170. Who he was. Com. ibid.

Pius, disciple of Saint James, appointed by him as the first bishop of Seville. Dex. and Com. A.D. 37, no. 8. He suffers martyrdom. Dex. A.D. 60.

Placentia, formerly Ambracia. See Ambracia.

Placentia, a city of Cantabria, founded by the people of Placentia. Dex. A.D. 384.

Placidia Augusta, daughter of Theodosius. Dex. A.D. 407, and Appendix, A.D. 430.

Placidus, martyr of Mantua, flourishes at Lisbon. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 22. He suffers martyrdom with his companions at Mantua-Carpetana. Dex. A.D. 353.

The plagues that afflicted the Spains at the entry of the Goths: to what extent were they foretold through Jeremiah and Zechariah? Com. A.D. 424, no. 1.

The story of Plautilla, Paul’s disciple. Com. A.D. 66, no. 16.

Pliny the Younger, a kinsman of Antonia Maximilla, disciple of Saint Andrew. Dex. A.D. 100; Com. no. 23. Converted to the faith, he suffers martyrdom. Dex. A.D. 220. He flourishes. Dex. A.D. 112.

Plutarch, the moral philosopher, flourishes. Dex. A.D. 122.

When did Polycarp the martyr come to Rome? Dex. and Com. A.D. 156, no. 1.

Polycarp, martyr in Asia. Dex. and Com. A.D. 170.

Polycrates, a distinguished bishop in Asia. Dex. A.D. 198.

Polyxena, disciple of Saint Andrew. Dex. A.D. 71, and Com. ibid., no. 2. Her deeds. Com. ibid. She dies peacefully in Spain. Dex. A.D. 100; Com. no. 81.

The people of Pamplona converted to the faith through the work of Saint Saturninus, numbering forty thousand. Com. A.D. 76, no. 2. Many others also through the preaching of Saint Firminus. Com. A.D. 110, no. 3. He preaches there. Saint Honestus, presbyter. Ibid. Martyrs. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 62.

Correction of a passage of Pomponius Mela. Com. A.D. 52. His homeland. See Mellaria.

Pomponius Paulatus, bishop of Toledo. Dex. A.D. 245. Of very noble birth. Com. ibid. He writes to Saint Licerius. Dex. A.D. 268; Com. no. 8. Concerning him. Dex. A.D. 285. He dies. Dex. A.D. 286. See Dex. A.D. 430, no. 10.

Pontius Pilate. See Pilate.

Pontius Paulinus, bishop of Embrun, receives the bodies of the holy martyrs Vincent and Orentius. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 24.

Pontius Paulinus of Nola, bishop. See Paulinus.

Porphyrius, disciple of Saint Catherine, suffers martyrdom. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 60.

Thirty Catholic writers attack Porphyry the philosopher and apostate in their writings. Dex. A.D. 310.

The Church of Portucale, or Porto, established by Saint Peter of Braga, with Basil, disciple of Saint James, appointed there as its first bishop. Com. A.D. 36, no. 2.

Potamia, martyr of Tarragona, with her companions. Com. A.D. 360, no. 4.

The prefecture of the praetorium: what kind of dignity was it, and how great? Com., letter to Orosius, section “After he had come from the East.” The kinds of prefectures. Ibid. The ancient formula for the praetorian prefects. Ibid. Prefigured in Joseph the patriarch. Ibid. Called “patriarch” and “father of the empire.” Ibid. By some considered greater than the emperor’s chief steward. Ibid. The praetorian prefects Dexter and Cynegius, both Spaniards. Ibid.

Praetextatus, bishop of Barcelona, attended the Council of Iliberris. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5.

Presbyters left in Spain by the apostle Paul. Dex. A.D. 60.

The primacy of the Church of the Spains: why was it in Toledo, and when was it established? Dex. and Com. A.D. 105, no. 6. Where, according to the Apostolic Canons, are primates of the Church to be established? Com. ibid.

Primitivus, martyr, brother of Saint Facundus. Dex. A.D. 139. His deeds. Com. ibid.

Primitivus, martyr of Zaragoza. Com. A.D. 300, no. 50.

Priscilla, wife of Aquila Ponticus and disciple of Paul, suffers martyrdom. Dex. A.D. 95.

The birth, character, and perversity of intellect of Priscillian. Dex. and Com. A.D. 380, no. 2, and A.D. 382. His punishment. Dex. A.D. 388.

Probus the Spaniard, converted by Paul. Dex. A.D. 64. He sits as pontiff at Ravenna and dies. Dex. A.D. 100; Com. no. 13.

Probus, emperor. Dex. A.D. 277.

Probus, martyr of Salamanca, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 430.

Prochorus, disciple of the apostle Saint John and historian of his deeds. Dex. A.D. 94.

Proculus, martyr of Interamna in Spain. Com. A.D. 160, no. 2, and Dex. A.D. 175.

Proculus, martyr of Serpa, with a companion. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 2.

When the provinces of the world were assigned by lot among the apostles. Com. A.D. 34, no. 10.

The Spanish province of Carthaginensis divided into two. Dex. A.D. 419.

Prudentius, Spanish poet: where and when was he born? Dex. and Com. A.D. 380, no. 7. He becomes governor of Toledo, Córdoba, and Zaragoza. He also becomes a commander. He flourishes in poetry and rhetoric. Dex. A.D. 388. He seeks Rome. Ibid. He flourishes there. Dex. A.D. 396, where his writings are discussed. He writes against Symmachus, and why? Com. A.D. 417, no. 1. He returns to Spain and writes there. Com. A.D. 423, no. 2, and A.D. 424. He dies in the church of Saint Mary of the Column at Zaragoza. Ibid.

Prudentius, bishop of Lérida, sends Orosius to Africa. Dex. and Com. A.D. 400, no. 2.

Publius, martyr of Zaragoza, one of the eighteen companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 50. [Col. 1263]

Three boys of Pamplona suffer martyrdom with Bishop Valens. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 62.

Pupienus, emperor. Dex. A.D. 240 and 241.

Pynetus of Crete flourishes. Dex. A.D. 174.

Pyramus, king of Gaul. Dex. A.D. 284.

Pymenius. See Pimenius.

Pyonius. See Pionius.

## Q

Forty philosophers converted by Saint Catherine suffer martyrdom. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 60.

Quadratus, a disciple of the apostles, writes an Apology in defense of the faith. Dex. A.D. 128.

Quadratus, bishop of Ulia. Dex. A.D. 139.

Quartus preaches in Spain and dies there. Dex. A.D. 50; Com. no. 5; and Dex. A.D. 105.

Quincianus, under whom Agatha suffered, and his son Quincianus. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 29.

Quinctius, bishop of Toledo. Com. A.D. 182, no. 5, and Dex. A.D. 208 and 222.

Quintus Quintilius, emperor. Dex. A.D. 273.

Quintilian of Calagurris, rhetorician. Com. A.D. 90, at the end.

Quiricus, bishop of Toledo, author of the hymn concerning Saint Eulalia of Barcelona. Com. A.D. 300, no. 52. He introduced a community of monks into his church. Ibid., in the hymn.

Quiricus and Julita, martyrs. See Julita.

Quiriulus, martyr of Évora, with his companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 20.

Quiteria, a Spanish virgin and martyr, and her deeds. Com. A.D. 138, no. 5. Her companions, martyrs. Ibid.

## R

Centolla, daughter of Ragonis Quinctianus, virgin and martyr. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 29.

Rebecca, also called Sarra, companion of Polyxena the virgin and disciple of Saint Andrew. Dex. and Com. A.D. 71, no. 2.

Recaredus, king of Spain, in whom the monarchy of Spain was founded. See the Appendix to A.D. 430.

Regula, virgin and martyr, companion of Saint Felix. Dex. A.D. 285.

Regulus, converted to the faith in Gallaecia. Dex. A.D. 60; Com. no. 6.

The relics of Saint Stephen discovered. Com. A.D. 400, no. 2.

How the relics of the saints in Spain were guarded by Christians during the barbarian invasion. Com. A.D. 423, no. 6, in chapter 3 of the Acts of the Council of Braga.

Restitutus, presbyter of Ilipula, attended the Council of Iliberris. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5. He suffers martyrdom with his companions. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 33.

Revocata, martyr of Argenteola, with her companions. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 36.

Revocata, virgin and martyr of Viana, with her companions. Dex. A.D. 260.

Rhoda, a city—which one? Com. A.D. 300, no. 44. Its martyrs. Dex. ibid.

Riparius, a Spanish presbyter, meets Saint Jerome in opposition to Vigilantius. Com. A.D. 388, no. 11.

Rixius-Varus, or Ricius-Varus, governor, converted to the faith. By whom? Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 3.

Many Roman pontiffs. Dex. A.D. 260 and 296, and A.D. 308; Com. no. 25. Spaniards also included under the name “Romans.” Com. A.D. 35, no. 3, and Com. A.D. 37, no. 5.

Romulus, martyr and chamberlain of Trajan. Dex. and Com. A.D. 100, no. 2.

Romulus, martyr of Concordia. Com. A.D. 145, no. 2.

Roses that arose every year by divine power at the tomb of the martyrs of Córdoba. Com. A.D. 138, no. 5.

Rufina, virgin and martyr of Seville, with her sister Justa. Com. A.D. 300, no. 48.

Rufinianus, Baetican martyr, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 15.

Rufinus, martyr of Seville, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 115.

Rufinus, Baetican martyr, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 15.

Rufinus, formerly an advocate, becomes a bishop. Com. A.D. 388, no. 4, and Dex. A.D. 407.

Rufus, disciple of the apostles and son of Simon of Cyrene, sits as bishop at Dertosa, or Tortosa. Dex. and Com. A.D. 100, no. 4, and Dex. A.D. 112.

Rufus, a bishop greatly deceived. Dex. and Com. A.D. 424, no. 6.

Rusticus Bolanus, consul at Rome, a Spaniard. Dex. A.D. 116.

The noble family of the Rustici in Spain. Com. ibid. Rusticus Antistius praised by Martial. Ibid.

Rutilius, an African martyr, comes to Córdoba. Dex. A.D. 110. He suffers martyrdom. Dex. A.D. 116.

## S

Sabina, virgin and martyr of Mérida, suffered martyrdom at Agaunum. Dex. and Com. A.D. 300, no. 1.

Sabina, a virgin of Ávila, suffered martyrdom with her brothers. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 54.

Sabinus, bishop, sent with his colleague Felix to Cyprian. Com. A.D. 255, no. 2.

Sabinus, bishop of Seville, attended the Council of Iliberris. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5. Two prelates of that name and see. Ibid.

Saint Vincent suffered martyrdom on the shore at Saguntum. Com. A.D. 300, no. 51.

Salaria, a city of Lusitania—which one? Com. A.D. 230, no. 2. Its martyrs. Dex. ibid.

The Salazarian family honors Saint Lawrence as a kinsman. Com. A.D. 246.

Salia Vetus, of which Prudentius accuses himself of having forgotten—what was it? Com. A.D. 380, no. 7.

Saint Juvencus the presbyter died at Salamanca. Dex. A.D. 337 and 407.

The martyrs of Salamanca killed by the Vandals. Dex. A.D. 430.

Salvia Terra, a city of Cantabria—which one? Com. A.D. 430, no. 8. The relics of Saint Theodosia were brought there. Dex. ibid.

The noble contest of the Samaritan woman of the Gospel, and of her sons and sisters. Com. A.D. 60.

Sampyrus, bishop of Astorga, wrote a history of Spain. First part, Apology, § 1.

Sarra, a virgin and disciple of Saint Andrew, comes to Spain. Dex. and Com. A.D. 71, no. 2.

Saturninus, bishop of Toulouse, was a disciple of the apostle Saint Peter. Com. A.D. 76, no. 2. He preaches at Pamplona, and with what success? Ibid. He preaches at Toledo. Dex. ibid. He preaches again at Toledo. Dex. A.D. 112.

Saturninus, martyr of Viana, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 260.

Saturninus, martyr of Deiobriga, with a companion. Dex. A.D. 285.

Saturninus, martyr of Clunia, with 355 companions. Dex. A.D. 290.

Saturninus, martyr of Patavonium, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 34.

Saturninus, martyr of Argenteola, with his companions. Dex. ibid.
