The four martyrs named Saturninus of Zaragoza: why were they so called? Com. A.D. 300, no. 50.

The Sarmatian war. Dex. A.D. 122.

Saxi-Firmum, a city. See Sexifirmum.

A rock is opened by divine power to conceal Saint Mary the servant. Com. A.D. 360, no. 7.

Satyrus, martyr of Juliobriga, with his companions. Com. A.D. 360, no. 3.

The city of Scalabis, and its citizens and martyrs. Com. A.D. 277, no. 2.

Writers against Porphyry. See Porphyrius. Against Julian the Apostate. Dex. A.D. 368.

Sebastianus, a Spanish military commander, martyr under Nero. Com. A.D. 60, no. 1.

Sebastianus of Milan, a most renowned martyr: whom did he bring to the faith? Dex. and Com. A.D. 290.

Sebastianus, bishop of Salamanca, wrote a history of Spain. First part, Apology, § 1.

Secundianus, martyr of Concordia. Com. A.D. 145, no. 2.

Secundinus, bishop of Castulo, attended the Council of Iliberris. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5.

Secundinus, martyr of Córdoba. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 57.

Secundus, disciple of Saint James and his doorkeeper, but made bishop by Saint Peter and sent back to the Spains. Dex. and Com. A.D. 37, no. 8, and Dex. A.D. 43 and 44. He was with Paul. Com. A.D. 52. Where did he preach? Dex. A.D. 100. His passion and translation. Com. ibid.

Secundus, martyr of Asti: where was he killed? Dex. and Com. A.D. 208, no. 8, and Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 31.

Secura, a city—which one? Com. A.D. 308, no. 13. Its martyr. Dex. ibid.

Sedulius, a celebrated poet, was bishop of Oretum. Dex. A.D. 428.

Segissama-Julia—which city? Com. A.D. 308, no. 1. Saint Brictius preaches there. Dex. ibid.

Segissamona, a city—which one? Com. A.D. 300, no. 64. Its martyr. Dex. ibid.

Segissamunculum. See Com. A.D. 308, no. 1.

How the bishop of Segorbe used this chronicle. First part, Apology, § 2.

The first bishop of Segovia was Saint Hierotheus. See under Hierotheus.

Selambina, a city—which one? Com. A.D. 300, no. 5. Its presbyter Sylvanus attended the Council of Iliberris.

Senagris, bishop of Braga, also attended there. Ibid.

Seneca the Christian died at Sintria—which Seneca was this? Dex. and Com. A.D. 50, no. 6.

The letters of Seneca to Paul: what were they? Dex. and Com. A.D. 64. Whether he adhered to the Christian faith. Com. ibid. He dies. Dex. A.D. 66; Com. no. 17.

Many old men of truly astonishing age in the primitive Church. Com. A.D. 66, no. 2.

Sentica, a city—which one? Com. A.D. 356, no. 4. Its martyrs. Dex. ibid.

Seoris, a city—which one? Also called Saria. Com. A.D. 300, no. 50. Its martyrs. Dex. ibid.

Sepharad, in Hebrew **סְפָרַד**, is Spain. Com. A.D. 37, no. 5, at the end.

The seven brother martyrs, sons of Saint Symphorosa. Dex. A.D. 100; Com. no. 24.

Septentrius, disciple of Saint Caecilius, suffered martyrdom with him at Granada. Com. A.D. 57.

Serapion, lector of Saint Theodorus, bishop of Zaragoza, suffered martyrdom with him. Dex. A.D. 71.

Serapion of Clunia, martyr with his companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 63.

Serena, wife of Stilicho, a Spaniard, whose praises Claudian sang. Com. A.D. 388, no. 9.

Serenus Grannius writes to Hadrian Caesar on behalf of the Christians. Dex. A.D. 130.

Sergius of Clunia, martyr with his companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 63.

Serpa, a city in Baetica, and its martyrs. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 2.

Serranus. See Asturius Serrenus.

Servandus, martyr of Mérida, with a companion. Com. A.D. 298.

Servilia, a Roman Christian woman. Dex. A.D. 86.

Setavis, a city—which one? Com. A.D. 66, no. 3. Its martyrs. Dex. ibid.

Severinus, martyr of Juliobriga, with his companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 19.

Severinus, martyr of Iturissa, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 45.

Severus, emperor. Dex. A.D. 195, 200, 202, and 208. He dies. Dex. A.D. 213.

Severus, bishop and martyr of Barcelona. Dex. A.D. 285. Two men of that name. Com. ibid. and First part, Apology, § 2. See also Dex. and Com. A.D. 252, no. 3.

Severus, Baetican martyr, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 15.

Severa, mother of the holy martyrs Vincent and Laetus. Dex. A.D. 352.

Severus, bishop of Lamacum, a writer. Dex. A.D. 388.

Severus, bishop of Minorca, converts the Jews to the faith. Com. A.D. 424, no. 11.

Sexifirmum, a city—which one? Com. A.D. 50, no. 3, and Com. A.D. 100, no. 5.

Sextus the philosopher flourishes. Dex. A.D. 122.

Sidonius, or Sydonius, Apollinaris writes against Vigilantius. Com. A.D. 388, no. 11.

Sigeric, king of the Goths. Com. A.D. 430, at the end.

Sihignia, a city—which one? Com. A.D. 356, no. 2, and Dex. with Com. A.D. 366, no. 1. Its saints. Dex. in both years.

Sila, nurse of the nine virgins and martyrs. Com. A.D. 138, at the end.

Silo, king of Spain, writes to Cyxillanus, bishop of Toledo. Com. A.D. 286, no. 2, in Saint Thyrsus.

Simon the apostle sets out to preach. Dex. and Com. A.D. 41.

The tricks of Simon Magus. Com. A.D. 91, no. 3.

The deeds of Simon of Cyrene. Dex. and Com. A.D. 112, no. 10, and those of his sons. See under the entries Alexander and Rufus.

The port and city of Sines: where are they? Com. A.D. 263. Its saints. Dex. ibid.

Sinesius, bishop, suffers martyrdom at Nertobriga with a companion. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 22. Their acts. Com. ibid. [Col. 1266]

Pope Siricius. See Syricius.

Sirmium, a city—which one? Com. A.D. 100, no. 5. Its martyrs. Dex. ibid.

Solia, a city—which one? Its presbyter Eumantius attended the Council of Iliberris. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5.

The martyr of Solia. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 28.

Socrates, martyr of Iturissa, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 45.

Three suns seen in Spain at the time of the Lord’s Nativity. Dex. and Com. A.D. 2. Where other similar apparitions are discussed.

An eclipse of the sun at the death of Augustus Caesar. Dex. A.D. 15. Another at Christ’s death. Dex. A.D. 34; Com. no. 1. Another at the beginning of Nero’s reign. Dex. and Com. A.D. 60. Another, also great. Dex. A.D. 350.

Pope Soter. Dex. A.D. 171.

Soter, a Roman virgin and martyr: where did she suffer martyrdom? Dex. and Com. A.D. 300, no. 37.

Spiridion, bishop of Toledo, a distinguished confessor. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 32.

Splendonius, bishop of Ambracia, or Placentia, expels the Priscillianists from the city. Dex. A.D. 424.

Stacteus. See Getulius.

Statius Papinius, to whom he dedicated Book IV of the *Silvae*. Dex. and Com. A.D. 110, no. 7.

The killing of Stephen the Protomartyr and the persecution that arose from it. See Persecution and Discovery. Com. A.D. 400, no. 2.

Stephen of Asti, martyr with his companions. Dex. A.D. 112.

Stephen of Clunia, martyr with his companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 63.

The praises of Stilicho the consul. Com. A.D. 388, no. 9. His second consulship. Dex. A.D. 405.

Straton, Baetican martyr, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 15.

Successus, bishop from Eliocroca, attended the Council of Iliberris. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5.

Successus of Zaragoza, martyr, one of the eighteen companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 50.

Suellum, a town of Spain from which excellent javelin-throwers came. Dex. A.D. 86 and 430.

The Council of Suessanum in the case of Pope Marcellinus. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 18. Which fathers attended there? Ibid.

The Sueves occupy Gallaecia, after Lusitania has been devastated. Dex. A.D. 423. Concerning them again. Dex. A.D. 424. They are Daniel’s third beast. Appendix to A.D. 430. The kings of the Sueves. Ibid.

Sussana, virgin and martyr of Iria Flavia. Dex. and Com. A.D. 300, no. 15.

Sussana, virgin and martyr of Braga. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 8.

Sussana, martyr of Clunia, with her companions. Dex. ibid., no. 10.

Sussana, virgin and martyr of Carthage, with her companions. Dex. and Com. A.D. 308, no. 7.

Sylvanus, presbyter of Selambina, attended the Council of Iliberris. Com. A.D. 300, no. 5, and Com. A.D. 308, no. 7.

Sylvester of Braga, martyr. Dex. A.D. 300; Com. no. 20.

Pope Sylvester, under whom the Church flourished anew. Dex. A.D. 308; Com. no. 25. He instituted the feast of the Discovery of the Holy Cross. Dex. A.D. 424.

The Apostles’ Creed: in what year was it composed by them? Com. A.D. 41.

The Nicene Creed was dictated by Hosius of Córdoba. See Hosius. [Col. 1267]

Symphorosa, mother of the seven martyrs. Dex. A.D. 100; Com. no. 24. One of them restored to life through the agency of Saint John the apostle. Ibid.

Symphronius of Carthage, martyr with his companions. Com. A.D. 300, no. 63, and Com. A.D. 270, no. 2.

Pope Syricius. Dex. A.D. 388 and 398.

## T.

Tacitus, emperor. Dex. A.D. 277. Tades: which city? Dex. A.D. 308, Com. no. 13. A river of the same name. There, in Com., the Tagonium River is quite different from the Tagus. Dex. and Com. A.D. 308 no. 6. Tagora, or Tagura, a city of Africa. Com. A.D. 360 no. 4. The Tanagrum River: where? Dex. and Com. A.D. 208 no. 8. A town of that name: which one? Dex. and Com. A.D. 360 no. 9. The Church of Tarragona established by St. James, with Agathodorus appointed there as its first bishop. Dex. and Com. A.D. 37 no. 8. He dedicates a shrine to the Blessed Virgin. Dex. A.D. 38. Epaphroditus, the second bishop, appointed by St. Peter. See Epaphroditus. Martyrs under Nero. Dex. A.D. 60. Under other rulers. Dex. and Com. A.D. 268 no. 4, and Com. A.D. 300 no. 26, and Com. A.D. 308 no. 18, and Dex. A.D. 360. Bishops of that province were present at the Council of Nicaea. Dex. A.D. 324. A council under Bishop Himerius, in the time of Pope Siricius. Com. A.D. 388 no. 10. The city destroyed by the barbarians. Dex. A.D. 424. Its noble citizen Paulus Orosius. See Orosius. Tarsis. See Tharsis. Tartesia, the same as Tarsis. See Tharsis. Tela: which city? Com. A.D. 290 no. 3. Its martyrs. Dex. ibid. and A.D. 299. Marcellus, bishop. Dex. A.D. 382. A synod. Dex. A.D. 424, where Domitian, bishop, is discussed. The church of St. Mary of the Column at Caesaraugusta, established by St. James, is proved. Com. A.D. 37 no. 3, etc. It is enlarged. Com. A.D. 312. Its festival. Dex. A.D. 52. To what extent it was the first. Com. A.D. 37 no. 3. That of St. Mary at Braga, established by the same man. Hugo of Porto, among the Author’s Eulogies. That of St. James established at Venice. Com. A.P. 41 no. 4. The one at Compostela: by whom? Com. A.D. 42. The most celebrated temple of the Egyptian Hercules on the island of Gades among the pagans. Com. A.D. 66 no. 22. One erected to St. Vincent the Levite at his body. Com. A.D. 300 no. 51. That of St. Eulalia of Barcelona. Ibid. and Com. A.D. 312. That of Saints Vincent, Sabina, and Christeta. Com. A.D. 312. That of St. Leocadia, virgin. Ibid. That of Saints Vincent and Laetus. Dex. A.D. 353. That of St. Thyrsus of Toledo, erected by Cyxillane. See Tyrsus. The church of Toledo enlarged by Olympius II. Dex. A.D. 424. Churches built everywhere through the agency of Hosius, at the command of Constantine and Helena. Dex. and Com. A.D. 312. Terasia, or Tarasia, wife of St. Paulinus, a Spaniard renowned for holiness. Com. A.D. 396 no. 1. The earthquake at Christ’s death. Com. A.D. 34. Another at Rome. Dex. and Com. A.D. 60. Tertullian flourishes. Dex. A.D. 208 no. 9. His testimony concerning St. Rutilius. See Rutilius. Tertullus, martyr of Évora, with his companions. Com. A.D. 300 no. 20.

[Col. 1267] Tetricus led in triumph. Dex. and Com. A.D. 276 no. 2. Where Tharsis was located is discussed at length. Com. A.D. 66 no. 22. What is said of it in the sacred writings? Ibid. It is wrongly confused by some with Ophir. Ibid. The theater of Pompey burned down. Dex. and Com. A.D. 23. Theodoredus, king of the Goths. Dex. A.D. 430 at the end, and in the Appendix to that year. Theodoretus aptly interprets Daniel’s prediction concerning the time of the apostles’ preaching in Jerusalem. Com. A.D. 36. Theodore, disciple of St. James. Dex. and Com. A.D. 37 no. 8. He is placed in charge of the Church of the Column. Dex. A.D. 41. Where does he preach? Dex. and Com. A.D. 50. He becomes bishop of Caesaraugusta and suffers martyrdom. Dex. and Com. A.D. 71 no. 5. Theodore, martyr of Huesca, with Philippa. Dex. A.D. 138. Theodore the Admirable, surnamed Trichinas, hermit of Medellín. Dex. and Com. A.D. 300 no. 46. Theodore of Clunia, martyr with his companions. Com. A.D. 300 no. 63. Theodore, martyr of Seville, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 308, Com. no. 16. Theodoriscus of Clunia, martyr with his companions. Com. A.D. 300 no. 63. Theodosia, martyr of Tarragona, with her companions. Dex. A.D. 300, Com. no. 26. The relics of Theodosia, virgin and martyr of Caesarea, brought to Cantabria. Dex. A.D. 430. Theodosius, second bishop of Barcelona. Dex. A.D. 94, 100, and A.D. 285. Theodosius, martyr of Tela, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 290. Theodosius, father of the emperor Theodosius. Dex. A.D. 382. He becomes a martyr. Dex. A.D. 423. Theodosius the Great, a Spaniard, emperor. Dex. A.D. 382. He restores religion in the East. Ibid. no. 10. He attends the council of Milan. Dex. A.D. 384. He was entered by the Greeks in the Catalogue of the Saints. Com. A.D. 382. Theodosius the Younger, emperor. Dex. A.D. 424. The wondrous conversion to God of Theodosius, a Spanish Jew. Dex. and Com. A.D. 424 no. 11. Theonas, martyr of Iturissa, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 300, Com. no. 45. Theophilus of Seville, martyr with his companions. Com. A.D. 115. Theophilus of Viana, martyr with his companions. Dex. A.D. 260. Theophilus of Argenteola, martyr with his companions. Dex. A.D. 300, Com. no. 36. Theopompus, martyr of Nertobriga, with his companion. Dex. A.D. 300, Com. no. 59. Theoprepes, son of Saints Philetus and Laeda, martyr of Barcelona. Com. A.D. 138 no. 2. The name Theresa derived from St. Thyrsus the martyr and applied to women. Com. A.D. 285, after no. 10. Also Tarasia, or Terasia. Thermancia, wife of the emperor Honorius, a Spaniard. Com. A.D. 417 no. 1. Thermeda, a city of Carpetania: which one? Com. A.D. 290 no. 1. Its martyrs. Dex. ibid. and A.D. 308, Com. no. 6. Thesiphon, disciple of St. James and ordained lector by him. Dex. and Com. A.D. 37 no. 8. But made bishop by St. Peter and sent back to the Spains. Com. ibid. and Dex. A.D. 43 and 44.

[Col. 1268] Where does he preach? Dex. A.D. 54 no. 10. He suffers martyrdom with St. Caecilius. See Caecilius. Thiar, a city: which one? Dex. A.D. 353. Its citizen Gratianus, bishop. Ibid. The apostle Thomas sets out to preach. Dex. and Com. A.D. 41. Thomas de Torralba of the Society of Jesus, discoverer of this Chronicle. First Apology, p. 1, § 1. Thraseas was a Christian poet. Dex. A.D. 86. Tiberius adopted by Augustus. Dex. and Com. A.D. 2 no. 2. His victories. Dex. and Com. A.D. 9. He begins his reign. Dex. A.D. 15. See Pilate. Tile, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 116 no. 3. Its martyr. Dex. ibid. Whether Timothy attended the Virgin’s funeral. Com. A.D. 48. He comes to Spain with Paul. Dex. A.D. 64 and Com. A.D. 66. Titianus, prefect of the praetorium. Dex. and Com. A.D. 347. Titulcia, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 308 no. 6. Its martyred abbots. Dex. ibid. Titus Livius dies. Dex. and Com. A.D. 19. Titus, Paul’s disciple, attended his martyrdom. Com. A.D. 66 no. 16. His acts and preaching in Spain. Dex. A.D. 220 no. 3. Titus, presbyter of Vinc, attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300 no. 5. By whom Toledo was founded. Com. A.D. 37 no. 5. The Jews of Toledo did not consent to Christ’s death. Com. A.D. 35 no. 7. The Church of Toledo established by St. James, with St. Elpidius appointed as its first bishop. Dex. and Com. A.D. 36. He consecrates the church to the Blessed Virgin. Dex. A.D. 38. Marcus the Gnostic heretic expelled from Toledo. Dex. A.D. 169. Councils. See under the word Council. Martyrs. Dex. A.D. 300, Com. nos. 48, 50, 52, and A.D. 352. Bishops. See under the names Elpidius, Julianus, Hermolaus, Honoratus, Eugenius, Pelagius, Patruinus, Turibius, Quinctius, Vincentius, Pomponius, Paulatus, Melantius, Natalis, Olympius I and II, Gregorius, Audentius, Asturius, Majorinus, Fetadius, Isicius, Castinus, Paternus, etc. A catalogue printed by Loaysa, greatly abridged. Com. A.D. 424 no. 7. Vincent of Córdoba flourished there. Dex. A.D. 360. Governors and duumvirs. See under the names Aulus Cornelius Palma, P. Turanus, Dexter, Prudentius the poet. Torisia, a city, the same as Tucci. See Tucci. Torpes, a noble martyr of Pisa, miraculously brought to Spain. Dex. and Com. A.D. 263. Torquatus, disciple of St. James, made exorcist by him but sent into Spain as a bishop by Blessed Peter. Com. A.D. 37 and Dex. A.D. 43 and 44. Where does he preach? Dex. A.D. 52. His writings. Dex. A.D. 66, Com. no. 4. Where are his arm and heart preserved incorrupt? There is discussion of the miracle customarily performed each year at his tomb. Ibid. Trajan born in Spain. Com. A.D. 100 no. 2. He becomes emperor. Dex. A.D. 101. His deeds. Ibid. and A.D. 104, 105, and 115. Treuga, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 105 no. 5 with Dexter. Priscillian punished at Trier with his companions. Dex. A.D. 388.

[Col. 1269] Tricium-mellatum: which city? Com. A.D. 368 no. 1. Several councils held there. Dex. ibid. At Trident, Maxentia of Coria flourishes. Dex. A.D. 419. She was the mother of St. Vigilius, bishop. Com. Trophimus, martyr of Uxama-Barca. Dex. A.D. 91. Tucci, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 308 no. 17. Its martyrs. Dex. ibid. The Church of Tuy founded by St. Peter, bishop of Braga. See Peter of Braga. Its first bishop, St. Epitacius. See Epitacius. Martyrs. Dex. A.D. 300, Com. no. 25, and A.D. 424. The Tugiensis woodland: what is it, and by whom was it evangelized? Dex. A.D. 100. Turanus, duumvir of Toledo. Dex. A.D. 105. Turbula, a city: which one? Dex. and Com. A.D. 255 no. 4. Its martyr. Ibid. Turibius of Toledo, bishop: what sort of man? Dex. A.D. 182. Irenaeus dedicates his books to him. Ibid. and in Com. Turibius, father of Saints Vincent and Laetus, martyrs. Dex. A.D. 352. Turibius, bishop of Astorga, presides over the Council of Toledo. Com. A.D. 386 no. 1. Turigium, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 285 no. 7. Its martyrs. Dex. ibid. and in Com. Turillus, disciple of St. Isicius, suffers martyrdom at Granada. Com. A.D. 57. Turrinus, presbyter of Castulo, attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300 no. 5. Tynius Rufus, governor of Palestine. Dex. A.D. 135. Thyrsus the martyr: although born at Toledo, he was killed at Apollonia; this is defended at length after Com. A.D. 286 no. 2.

## U

Ulia, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 139 no. 3. Its bishop, St. Quadratus. Dex. ibid. Victor, presbyter, attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300 no. 5. The Church of Lisbon established by St. Peter of Braga. See Olyssiponensis. Ulpian, the jurist, flourishes. Dex. A.D. 228. Unda, or Undumenum, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 105 no. 3. St. Valentinus, bishop. Ibid. in Dex. Urbanus of Caesaraugusta, martyr, one of the eighteen companions. Com. A.D. 300 no. 50. Cities formerly founded in the Spains by Jews. Com. A.D. 37 no. 5. By Greeks. See Amphilochius in Com. By Phoenicians. Under Gades, in Com. Urci: which city? Com. A.D. 54 no. 6. Its evangelizer. Dex. ibid. Januarius, its presbyter, attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300 no. 5. Urena, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 300 no. 2, where St. Valerius is discussed. Urgabona, a city, and the Urgabonense municipality. Com. A.D. 300 no. 55, and Dex. and Com. A.D. 308 no. 4. Martyrs. Ibid. Urias the prophet, father of St. Peter of Braga. Com. A.D. 37. Ursaona, now Osuna; its martyrs. Dex. and Com. A.D. 110 no. 8. Its citizen St. Natalis. See Natalis, bishop of Toledo. Utica, a city in Spain. Dex. and Com. A.D. 66 no. 6. Its martyrs. Dex. ibid. Leporius, its bishop. See Leporius. Urriculum, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 180 no. 2, with Dexter, and Dex. and Com. A.D. 308 no. 15. Martyrs. Ibid. Uxama-Argela, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 91 no. 1. Its bishop Exuperantius. Dex. A.D. 385. Uxama-Barca, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 91 no. 1. Its martyrs. Dex. ibid. and Com. A.D. 268 no. 4.

## V

Valens, bishop of Pompiliona, suffered with three boys. Dex. A.D. 300, Com. no. 62. The emperor Valens perishes in a fire. Dex. A.D. 382. The Church of Valencia established by St. James, with St. Eugenius I appointed its bishop. Dex. and Com. A.D. 37 no. 8. Its bishop, St. Victorius. See Victorius. Marcus the heretic expelled from Valencia of the Lusitanians. Dex. A.D. 169. Martyrs. Dex. A.D. 255. How many cities of that name are there? Com. ibid. The death of the emperor Valentinian. Dex. A.D. 375. Valentinus the heretic. Dex. A.D. 145. Valentinus, celebrated bishop of Viana. Dex. A.D. 424. Valentio was a martyr and companion of St. Pasicrates. Com. A.D. 168. See the Roman Martyrology, 25 May. Valerian, emperor. Dex. A.D. 257. He lives and dies miserably. Dex. A.D. 260. Valerius, bishop of Caesaraugusta, suffered much. Dex. and Com. A.D. 300 no. 2. He attended the Council of Illiberis with St. Vincent the Levite and Martyr. Com. ibid. no. 5. Another Valerius, bishop of Caesaraugusta, who attended the Council of Caesaraugusta. Dex. and Com. A.D. 384 no. 7. Another of the same name and see. Dex. A.D. 423. He is also found called Valerianus. Com. ibid. and Dex. A.D. 430. Valerius the Spaniard, who collected fragments of Berossus. Dex. A.D. 300, Com. no. 13. Vallata-Urbicua, a city of Spain: which one? Com. A.D. 255 no. 2. Its presbyter Felix wrote to St. Cyprian. Ibid. and in Dex. Varia, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 368 no. 1. Several synods convened there. Dex. ibid. Varinus, a Roman ecclesiastical writer. Dex. A.D. 285. How much Varro contributed to his country, according to Cicero’s testimony? First Apology, p. 1, § 3. The disciples of St. James called “seers” [vates]. Com. A.D. 54 no. 9. St. James the apostle preaches at Venice. Dex. A.D. 41. A temple is erected there in his honor. Com. ibid. Verenice (commonly Veronica) brought the holy face of the Lord to Rome. Dex. A.D. 48. Vergi, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 54 no. 10. Its bishop Cantonius attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300 no. 5. Vergilia, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 54 no. 10. Verissimus, martyr of Lisbon, with his sisters. Dex. A.D. 308, Com. no. 11. What does *vernulum* mean? Com. A.D. 286 no. 2, in the entry on St. Thyrsus. Verobisca, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 360 no. 7. Its martyr. Ibid. Veronica. See Verenice. The reign of Vespasian. Dex. and Com. A.D. 70. Veturius persecutes Christians. Dex. A.D. 300, Com. no. 11.

[Col. 1270] Vezozabia, a province: which one? Com. A.D. 290 no. 2. Its martyrs. Dex. ibid. Viana, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 260 no. 2. Martyrs. Dex. ibid. Confessor-bishops. Dex. A.D. 424. Vicensis, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 300 no. 8. Its bishop Justus. Dex. ibid. Another of the same name. Com. ibid. St. Lucianus transferred there. Dex. A.D. 308, Com. no. 8. Victor, son of the Samaritan woman, martyr. Com. A.D. 60 no. 1. Victor, martyr of Flaviobriga, with his companions. Dex. and Com. A.D. 182 no. 3. Victor, presbyter of Ulia, attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300 no. 5. Victor, martyr of Juliobriga, with his companions. Com. A.D. 300 no. 19. Victor, martyr of Iturissa, with his companions. Dex. A.D. 300, Com. no. 45. Victor, a Bracarensian catechumen and martyr. Dex. A.D. 300, Com. no. 61. Victor, Levite and martyr of Pax Augusta, with his companions. Com. A.D. 308 no. 24. Victor, son of the emperor Maximianus, is killed with his father. Dex. A.D. 388. Victoria, virgin and martyr of Córdoba. Com. A.D. 138 no. 6. Victoria, a Roman virgin and martyr, suffered martyrdom in Spain. Dex. A.D. 255. Victoria, martyr of Voluca, with her companions. Dex. A.D. 300, Com. no. 30. Victoria, widow and martyr of Illorci. Dex. A.D. 406. Victoricus, martyr of León, with his companions. Com. A.D. 298. Victorius, bishop of Valencia. Dex. A.D. 105. Victorius, presbyter of Egabrum, attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300 no. 5. Vigilantius the heretic, presbyter of Calagurris: whence did he come, from Gaul or from Spain? Dex. and Com. A.D. 388 no. 11. He corrupts the Church of Barcelona. Ibid. Villasicca, a city: which one? Com. A.D. 370 no. 3. Its citizen St. Asturius Serranus. Dex. ibid. Vinc, a city: which one? Its presbyter Titus attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300 no. 5. Vincentia, virgin and martyr of Coria. Dex. A.D. 424. Vincent, martyr of Aquae-Quintianae. Dex. A.D. 95. Vincent, martyr and bishop of Mevania. Dex. A.D. 200, Com. no. 40. Where did he suffer? Com. ibid. with Dex. Vincent, bishop of Toledo. Dex. A.D. 222 and 245. Two martyr-levites named Vincent, of Caesaraugusta: one of Huesca and one of Agen. Com. A.D. 300 no. 2, where the one of Agen is discussed. The one of Huesca attended the Council of Illiberis. Ibid. no. 5. A kinsman of Laurence. Com. A.D. 300, in the Appendix concerning him. Vincent, bishop of Ossonoba, attended the Council of Illiberis. Com. A.D. 300 no. 5. Vincent, martyr of Ávila, with his sisters. Dex. A.D. 300, Com. no. 54. Where were they born? This is investigated in Com. Vincent, martyr of Pax Augusta, with his companion. Dex. A.D. 308, Com. no. 24. Vincent, martyr of Toledo, with his twin brother. Dex. A.D. 352.

§ IV. A new and exact exposition of the same prophecy is proposed, concerning the incursions of the Alans, Vandals, Suebi, and Goths into Spain and concerning the Catholic monarchy, 580.

*Apologeticus* for Lucius Dexter against a recent opponent, 591.

Dedication letter, ibid.

The *Apologeticus* begins, ibid.

§ I. The purpose of the apology is disclosed, ibid.

§ II. How many and how great measures Pennottus had devised for blunting the authority of this *Chronicle*, 595.

§ III. Pennottus’ tripartite work is entangled in the same knots with which he attempts to bind Dexter’s entire history, 600.

§ IV. Certain inconsistencies of Pennottus, 604.

§ V. The rights of the Cistercian order, violated by Pennottus, are defended, 609.

§ VI. Blessed Abbot Joachim is defended against the slanders of Pennottus and others, 614.

§ VII. The objections raised by Pennottus against the *Chronicles* of Dexter and Maximus are answered, 627.

### PAULUS OROSIUS
Epistle of Dedication by Sig. Havercamp. 635  
Preface by Sig. Havercamp. 637  
Various dedications and prefaces. 613  
Gallandi’s notice on Paulus Orosius. 653  
Account of the orthography in the Longobardic manuscript of Orosius. 661  

# THE SEVEN BOOKS OF THE HISTORIES. 663

Preface to Aurelius Augustine. Ibid.

## BOOK ONE. 669

### CHAPTER ONE.

From whom the other historians began their histories, and from where he himself wishes to begin and how far he wishes to pursue his account. Ibid.

### CHAPTER II.

That the ancients divided the world into three parts. 672

### CHAPTER III.

On the Flood in the time of Noah. 697

### CHAPTER IV.

On Ninus and Semiramis. 699

### CHAPTER V.

That the region of the Pentapolis was struck from heaven and burned because of its unspeakable crimes of lust. 702

### CHAPTER VI.

Comparison of the disasters of Sodom and Rome. 704

### CHAPTER VII.

On the battle between the Telchines and the Carpathians and King Phoroneus; also on the flood of Achaea. 706

### CHAPTER VIII.

On the barrenness and famine of Egypt, for which Joseph provided a remedy, and on the vanity of the Egyptian priests. 709

On the flood in the time of the kings Amphictyon and Deucalion, the Ethiopian plague, and Liber Pater’s devastation of India. 712

On the people of God afflicted in Egypt, the ten plagues of the Egyptians, the crossing of the Arabian Gulf and its remaining traces; and on a certain destructive heat of the sun. 713

On the parricide of the Danaids, the cruelty of Busiris, and the story of Tereus, Procne, and Philomela; and on Perseus’s devastation of Asia. 718

### CHAPTER XII.

A collection of many crimes passed over in silence. 721

[Col. 1304]

### CHAPTER XIII.

The conflict between the Cretans and the Athenians, the Lapiths and the Thessalians. 722

### CHAPTER XIV.

Vesores, king of Egypt, attacks the Scythians in war and is defeated. The Scythians make Asia subject to themselves. 723

### CHAPTER XV.

The origin, customs, and deeds of the Amazons. 724

### CHAPTER XVI.

Epilogue to the history of the Amazons, in which he attacks the present blindness of the Romans. 728

### CHAPTER XVII.

The abduction of Helen and the destruction of Troy, with an admonition to the reader. 730

### CHAPTER XVIII.

Aeneas’s arrival in Italy and the various disasters of that same period. 731

On Sardanapalus, king of the Assyrians; on the Median kings Phraortes, Deioces, and Astyages; and on Cyrus, king of the Persians. 733

### CHAPTER XX.

The tyranny of Phalaris and the crimes of Aremulus, king of the Latins. 736

### CHAPTER XXI.

The war between the Peloponnesians and the Athenians; the incursions of the Amazons and Cimmerians into Asia; the prolonged siege and capture of Messene. The war of the Athenians against the Lacedaemonians; and of the Peloponnesians and Boeotians against the Athenians. 738

## BOOK TWO. 743

### CHAPTER ONE.

On the changes of kingdoms brought about by God’s providence. Ibid.

### CHAPTER II.

A kind of epilogue to the foregoing matters; a comparison of different kingdoms and periods, and on the alternation of kingdoms. 745

### CHAPTER III.

The beginning, condition, and state of the Babylonian and Roman kingdoms are almost alike, but their outcomes are different. 747

### CHAPTER IV.

On the founding of Rome and the period during which it obeyed the rule of kings. 749

### CHAPTER V.

The deeds of Brutus, the first consul; the war of the Tarquinians and Sabines; the secession of the plebs; famine and pestilence at Rome; and the war against the Veientes and Etruscans, in which that Fabian family perished. 753

### CHAPTER VI.

Cyrus devastates the East, captures Babylon, and defeats Croesus. 757

### CHAPTER VII.

Cyrus wages war against the Scythians and is defeated and killed by Tomyris. 761

### CHAPTER VIII.

Darius is put to flight by the Scythians; he conquers Asia, Macedonia, and the Ionians. He attacks the Athenians at the peril of his own life and that of many others. 762

### CHAPTER IX.

Xerxes is defeated by the Spartans under the command of Leonidas. 765

### CHAPTER X.

Themistocles puts Xerxes to flight after alienating the Ionians from him. 768

### CHAPTER XI.

Mardonius, while completing the remainder of the war, flees after losing his forces. Xerxes is killed. 770

### CHAPTER XII.

Rome is afflicted by a severe pestilence, while the wars are interrupted. On the war of the exiles and fugitives, and likewise of the Aequi and Volsci. 774

### CHAPTER XIII.

Famine and pestilence at Rome. Power is transferred from the consuls to the decemvirs, to the ruin of the state. Frequent earthquakes in Italy. The Fidenaean war. 775

### CHAPTER XIV.

On the rule of Sicily and the events that occurred there. 777

### CHAPTER XV.

The Athenians are attacked in the war of the Lacedaemonians, at the urging of Alcibiades. 781

### CHAPTER XVI.

The Athenians’ severe battles against the Lacedaemonians, their dreadful calamities, and the slaughter suffered by both sides. 783

Peace is granted to the Athenians under specified laws and conditions, and thirty rulers are appointed; they are expelled through the efforts of Thrasybulus. 786

### CHAPTER XVIII.

On the civil war between Artaxerxes and Cyrus, the sons of Darius, which ended in parricide. On the earthquake in Sicily and the formation of the island of Atalante. 790

[Col. 1305]

### CHAPTER XIX.

The Romans’ less than honorable siege of Veii. The city is captured and devastated by the Gauls. A comparison of that destruction with the present Gothic invasion. 792

## BOOK THREE. 795

Preface. Ibid.

### CHAPTER ONE.

On the peace made throughout Greece at the command of King Artaxerxes, and on the various wars waged before that peace by the Lacedaemonians against the king and the Thebans, including the story of Conon. 797

### CHAPTER II.

On the Lacedaemonians’ offense in Arcadia, the victory of the Thebans, and the death of Epaminondas, with an epilogue to the foregoing matters. 803

The earthquake of Achaea compared with that of Constantinople. The Romans capture several cities. 806

### CHAPTER IV.

On a most severe pestilence and its expiation. 807

### CHAPTER V.

A huge fissure in the earth appears in the middle of Rome. 808

The Romans overthrow and rout a vast multitude of Gauls; the Etruscans are defeated; and when the Gauls invade for the third time, they are slaughtered. Ibid.

The treaty of the Romans with the Carthaginians, a cause of many evils. It rains actual stones. Alexander the Great is born. The king of the Persians carries away Jewish captives. 810

A brief summary of the disasters of the wars that follow and were waged by the Romans. On the closing of the Gates of Janus. 811

### CHAPTER X.

Very many Roman matrons are accused and condemned for poisoning. 814

### CHAPTER XI.

Alexander, king of the Epirotes, is defeated and killed by the Samnites. 815

The deeds of Philip, king of Macedonia, and the peoples or cities he subdued. Ibid.

Philip besieges Byzantium without success. He attacks Scythia in war and conquers it. The Triballi snatch the booty from him. 822

The Samnites capture the Roman forces. The Romans break the treaty they had concluded and capture Satricum. 825

After Alexander’s death, his commanders divided the world among themselves and exhausted one another in mutual wars. 845

## BOOK FOUR. 853

Preface. Ibid.

### CHAPTER ONE.

On the war of the Tarentines, whom Pyrrhus assisted against the Romans. 857

The Romans are struck by a dreadful pestilence. A third war is waged against Pyrrhus: he is put to flight and perishes. 861

The Romans defeat the Tarentines with the aid of the Carthaginians and punish the eighth legion. 862

On certain dreadful prodigies and the Picentine war. 863

The deeds of the Romans against the Syracusans and Carthaginians, and the outcomes of various wars. The conspiracy of slaves and allies. 873

[Col. 1306]

The Carthaginians, having been denied peace, gather auxiliaries from everywhere and, under the leadership of Xanthippus, overthrow the Romans. They capture Regulus, and Aemilius and Fulvius avenge that injury. 878

### CHAPTER XXIII.

On the pitiable overthrow and destruction of Carthage. 915

On Sulla’s proscriptions and other cruel crimes. 972

On Crassus’s avarice, his operations against the Parthians, and his death. 1028

On the mutability of Roman power, as a kind of epilogue to the foregoing matters. 1029

On Caesar’s death and the disturbances and wars arising because of it. 1039

On Caesar Octavian Augustus and the deeds accomplished by him. 1042

On Antony’s deeds and the Battle of Actium. 1048

The life and deeds of Claudius Tiberius Caesar, and the very severe famine at Rome under him. 1072

On the rule, character, and crimes of Galba, Otho, and Vitellius. 1079

On the rule and deeds of Flavius Domitian Caesar. 1087

### CHAPTER XI.

The rule of Cocceius Nerva Caesar. 1088

The rule and deeds of Trajan. 1089

The rule of Hadrian. 1092

The rule of Antoninus Pius. 1094

The reigns of Commodus, Pertinax, and Didius Julianus. 1099
